description: Fought on February 8th 1814 on the same ground as Napoleon's victory at the Battle of Borghetto in 1796 resulted in an inconclusive engagement between the French under Eugène de Beauharnais and the Austrians under Field Marshal Heinrich von Bellegarde.

name: Battlefield of Nogent
description: On February 11th 1814, Victor's troops at Nogent held out admirably against those of Wittgenstein and Wrede, but as Wrede troops corssed the Sena river, the French abandonned Nogent to the Russians.

name: Battlefield of Gilly
description: The Prussian commanded by General Pirch on June 15th 1815, retreat had scarcely begun when his retreating columns were vigorously assaulted by four Squadrons de Service of the Imperial Guard commanded by General Letort.

name: General von Pirch tomb
description: He began his career in the Prussian army in 1775. At Waterloo Pirch handed over the command of II Corps to Prince Augustus of Prussia.

name: Gerhard von Scharnhorst tomb
description: He was a Prussian general and the most important military theorist and reformer of the Prussian army in the Napoleonic Wars.

name: Statue General Gerhard von Scharnhorst
description: He was a Prussian general and the most important military theorist and reformer of the Prussian army in the Napoleonic Wars.

name: Bust General Gerhard von Scharnhorst
description: He was a Prussian general and the most important military theorist and reformer of the Prussian army in the Napoleonic Wars.

name: Hesse Haus
description: House were it is said Genaral von Blücher stayed for on January 10th 1814.

name: Ottweiler old castle square
description: Place where the scene portrayed by Christian Sell for his 'Prince Blücher's address to the population, January 1814' in a series of historical postcards for the District Veterans' Association (Bezirkskriegerverband) in the early 20th century.

name: Battlefield of Heliópolis
description: French forces under General Kléber defeated the Ottoman army led by Nassif Pasha on March 20th 1800.

name: Battlefield of Alexandria
description: Also known as the Battle of Canope/Canopus. It was fought on March 21st 1801, where the British army and naval forces repelled an assault by the French army.

name: Siege of El Arish
description: The Siege of El Arish was a siege of the Ottoman fortress of El Arish by the French army, which took place from February 8th to 20th 1801 during the French campaign in Egypt.

name: Battlefield of Mandora
description: It was a minor battle fought on March 13th 1801 between French forces under François Lanusse and the British expeditionary corps under Ralph Abercromby.

name: Napoleon's monument
description: A pyramid-shaped memorial located directly in front of the Stella Maris Monastery on Mount Carmel. It commemorates French soldiers from Napoleon Bonaparte's army sick of the plague in 1799 and were burried there.

name: Siege of Acre
description: It was an unsuccessful French two month siege of the Ottoman city started on March 20th 1799 and was the turning point of Napoleon's invasion of Egypt and Syria

name: Battlefield of Lübeck
description: It took place on November 6th 1806 between soldiers of of Prussia led by Blücher, who were retreating from defeat at the Battle of Jena-Auerstedt, and French troops under Marshals Murat, Bernadotte, and Soult

name: Prise de Ratisbonne
description: Canvas by Johann Lorenz Rugendas the Younger. It depicts the storming of Ratisbon by the French army on April 23rd 1809 during the War of the Fifth Coalition.

name: Capture of Alexandria
description: On July 2nd 1798, the French army landed and took the city of Alexandria from the hands of the Janissaries.

name: Battlefield of Chebreiss
description: Also known as Shubra Khit,was the second major engagement of the French invasion of Egypt and Syria and took place on July 13th 1798.

name: Battlefield of Sediman
description: Also known as Battle of El Lahun, took place on October 7th 1798. French troops under General Louis Desaix defeated the Mamluk forces led by Murad Bey, securing control over Upper Egypt.

name: Battlefield of Jaffa
description: The French laid siege to the city of Jaffa, which was under Ottoman control. It was fought from March 3rd to the 7th 1799, when French forces managed to capture the city.

name: Battlefield of Mohrungen
description: On January 25th 1807, most of a First French Empire corps under the leadership of Marshal Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte fought a strong Russian Empire advance guard led by Major General Yevgeni Ivanovich Markov.

name: Battlefield of Allenstein
description: Also known as the Battle of Jonkowo and the Battle of Bergfriede. The battle on February 3rd 1807 resulted in a French field victory and allowed for a successful pursuit of the Russian army.

name: Bergfriede bridge - Allenstein
description: Towards the end of the afternoon, Soult, with the 24th Light and 4th Line regiments began his flanking attack and, after some ferocious combat, pushed the Russians beyond the Alle, capturing the Bergfriede bridge.

name: Napoleon's observation point - Allenstein
description: From the church tower, Napoleon observed the disposition of the main Russian army, spread between Jonkowo, Redykajny, and Gutkowo, which influenced his decision to avoid a general engagement (he had previously thought it was only a small detachment).

name: Napoleon's memorial - Allenstein
description: Napoleon's Memorial Stone in Olsztyn, next to Łyna (Alle) river, with a bilingual Polish and French inscription.

name: Olsztyn Marquet Square - Allenstein
description: At this square Napoleon received battle reports and commanded the battle of Allenstein.

name: Russian left wing- Allenstein
description: The left wing of the Russian army ended around this position.

name: Three Crosses Square in Olsztyn- Allenstein
description: Place of burial of French and Russian soldiers who died at the battle of Allenstein

name: Battlefield of Dürenstein (Krems)
description: Also known as he Battle of Krems. On November 11th 1805 a combined force of Russian and Austrian troops trapped a French division commanded by Théodore Maxime Gazan.

name: Little Frenchman Memorial - Dürenstein
description: French memorial to the soldiers who died at the battle of Dürenstein.

name: Battlefield of Sabugal
description: It was a meeting engagement of the Peninsular War which took place on April 3rd 1811 between Anglo-Portuguese forces under Arthur Wellesley (later the Duke of Wellington) and French troops under the command of Marshal André Masséna.

name: Wellington's Command Post - Bussaco
description: Wellington's command post during the battle.

name: Crauford's Command Post - Bussaco
description: General's Crauford command post during the battle.

name: Battlefield of Bussaco
description: It was fought on September 27th 1810 during the Peninsular War in the Portuguese mountain range of Serra do Buçaco, resulting in the defeat of French forces by Lord Wellington's Anglo-Portuguese Army.

name: Monument Battle of Bussaco
description: Constructed in 1873, the obelisk was greatly damaged by lightning in 1876 and was restored in 1878-1879.

name: Massena's Command Post - Bussaco
description: Remains of the windmill which served as Masséna's command post at Moura.

name: English Cemetery at Elvas
description: It is one of the oldest British Military Cemeteries in existence. It holds only five known graves but two of these for the tallen at Albuera and another for the fallen at Badajoz.

name: Lines of Torres Vedras
description: Lines of Torres Vedras were lines of forts and other military defences built in secrecy to defend Lisbon during the Peninsular War.

name: Duke of Wellington's Headquarters at Pero Negro
description: During the construction of the fortificaions of Lines of Arthur Wellesley established his headquarters at this residence.

name: Puente de Barba del Puerco
location: San Felices de los Gallegos, Salamanca
description: Uno de los cuatro cruces del río Águeda, fue volado en abril de 1811 por un ingeniero Portugués para cortar el paso a las tropas del General Marmont.

name: Wellington's Headquarters in Freineda
description: During the winters of 1811-1812 and 1812-1813, Wellington set his headquarters in a small Portuguese village about 25 kilometers from the Spanish border fortress of Ciudad Rodrigo.

name: Núcleo Interpretativo da Batalha da Roliça
description: Inaugurado a 17 de novembro de 2024 a memória do histórico confronto militar, ocorrido a 17 de agosto de 1808

name: French invasion of Malta
description: The French First Republic led by Napoleon Bonaparte successfully invaded the islands of Malta and Gozo, then ruled by the Knights Hospitaller, in June 10th 1798 as part of the Meiterranean 1798 of the French Revolutionary Wars.

name: General Vaubois landing point - Malta
description: On the morning of June 10th, the French began landing, General Vaubois landed between St. Julien and La Madelaine

name: General Desaix landing point - Malta
description: On the morning of June 10th, the French began landing, General Desaix landed at the eastern cost of the island.

name: General Bonaparte landing point - Malta
description: On the morning of June 10th, the French began landing, General Bonaparte landed nort-west of La Valeta.

name: French Memorial Fallen in Egypt Campaing
description: A memorial stone commemorating the French soldiers and participants of Napoleon's Egyptian Expedition located in the Latin Cemetery in Cairo.

name: Battle of Cape Santa María
description: A British squadron under the command of Commodore Graham Moore attacked and defeated a Spanish squadron led by Brigadier Don José de Bustamante.

name: Battle of Sandöström
description: The Swedes, whose fleet controlled the open sea, attempted to remove the Russian reinforcements.

name: Battle of Palva Sound
description: The Battle of Palva Sund was fought between Sweden and Russia on September 18th 1808.

name: Battlefield of Gamonal
description: On November 11th 1808, a French army under Soult overwhelmed the outnumbered Spanish troops under General Belvedere, opening central Spain, including Madrid, to invasion.

name: General Jirčik Memorial - Austerlitz
description: This memorial commemorates the soldiers of Jirčík's Brigade who were killed in the Battle of Austerlitz.

name: Bohdalice Palace
description: On November 29th 1805, Russian Tzar Alexander and Francis I Emperor of Austria spent the night at this venue, shortly before the Battle of Austerlitz.

name: Brno Obelisk
description: It was erected in 1818 to commemorate the end of long-lasting war miseries.

name: Šlapanice church
description: It was erected in 1818 to commemorate the end of long-lasting war miseries.

name: Zuran Hill - Austerlitz
description: Napoleon's command post during the battle of Austerlitz.

name: Santon Hill - Austerlitz
description: Here laid the left flank of the French army. The 17th Light Infantry Regiment, under the command of General Claparéde, was chosen for its defence.

name: Murat's HQ - Austerlitz
description: Before the Battle of Austerlitz, the place was utilized by French Marshal Murat as his headquartes. Later it was in hands of Prince Bagration who started his attack on the Santon Hill from here.

name: Action of 25 September 1806
description: A French squadron comprising five frigates and two corvettes, sailing to the French West Indies with supplies and reinforcements, was intercepted by a British squadron of six ships of the line.

name: Jeune Voltigeur - Toulouse battle
description: The work of artist Sonia Queija was inaugurated on February 15, 2025. The monument pays tribute to the soldiers who participated in the Battle of Toulouse in 1814.

name: Copenhagen (Wellington's horse) grave site
description: Copenhagen died on 12 February 1836 at Stratfield Saye, Duke of Wellington property at Hampshire in England, at the age of 28 years, and is burried under a large Turkey Oak tree.

name: Museo Storico Nazionale dell'Artiglieria
description: The Museo Storico Nazionale dell'Artiglieria is a museum in Turin, Italy, that houses a collection of military artillery from the Napoleonic era.

name: Friedland field hospital
description: During the Battle of Friedland, this building housed a hospital where wounded Russian soldiers were taken, and it is perhaps this building that L. N. Tolstoy describes in his novel War and Peace.

name: Friedland
location: Metropolitan Museum of Arts, New York
description: Friedland is a painting by the French artist Ernest Meissonier, depicting the Battle of Friedland in 1807. It is a gift of Henry Hilton to the Metropolitan Museum of Arts in 1887.

name: Napoleon in His Study at the Tuileries
description: Napoleon in His Study at the Tuileries is a painting by the French artist Jacques-Louis David, depicting Napoleon Bonaparte in his study at the Tuileries Palace in 1800. It is in the National Gallery of Art, West Building Main Floor, Gallery 56, in Washington D.C., USA.

name: Louis Bonaparte's tomb
description: Louis Bonaparte's tomb is in the Church of Saint-Leu-Saint-Gilles, Saint-Leu-la-Forêt, France. It is a sarcophagus in the choir of the church, and it is a gift of Napoleon Bonaparte to his brother Louis.

name: Kutuzov's bust at Friedland
description: Although Kutuzov did not took part in the Campaign in Poland there is a bust of him in the Russian town of Friedland, which is today Pravdinsk.

name: Vive l'Empereur!- Friedland
location: Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney
description: Jean Baptiste Édouard Detaille's magnificent Charge of the 4th Hussars at the battle of Friedland was purchased in 1893 by the Art Gallery of New South Wales and is exhibited at the Naala Nura, ground level, Grand Courts.

name: Russian soldiers memorial - Friedland
description: Dedicated to the Russian soldiers who fought in the Battle of Friedland in 1807, it was erected in 1992.

name: Napoleon's HQ after the battle of Friedland
description: Napoleon used this building as his HQ after the battle of Friedland in 1807.

name: Battle of Friedland
description: This artwork by Horace Vernet, represents Napoleon at the Battle of Friedland giving instructions to general Nicolas Oudinot. It is exhibited in the Hall of Battles in the Palace of Versailles.

name: Napoleon in Egypt
location: Princeton University Art Museum, Princeton, New Jersey
description: This artwork by Jean-Léon Gérôme, also called Napoleon in front of the Sphinx, represents Napoleon Bonaparte in Egypt.

name: Battlefield of Lodi
description: Fought on May 10th 1796, Bonaparte won a decisive victory against the Austrians.

name: Austrian position at Corte Palasio - Lodi
description: Sebotendorf located 2,100 infantes and 300 Austrian troopers near the villa of 'Corte Palasio' to protect a ford in the Adda river

name: Lodi - First action 9am
description: The French advance guard caught up with Josef Vukassovich's Austrian rear-guard at about 9 am on 10 May and after a clash followed them towards Lodi.

name: Neapolitan Cavlary position - Lodi
description: Sebottendorf had eight squadrons of Neapolitan cavalry at his disposal, Cavalry Regiments Re and Regina, and he positioned them around, just half hour form Lodi.

name: Lodi bridge
description: The iconic bridge over the Adda river where Napoleon gained the nickname 'Le Petit Caporal'.

name: Battlefield of Borghetto
description: On May 30th 1796, a French army led by General Napoleon Bonaparte forced a crossing of the Mincio River in the face of opposition from an Austrian army commanded by Feldzeugmeister Johann Peter Beaulieu.

name: Palazzo Guarienti
description: At the evening of the battle of Borghetto, Napoleon lodged at this building and was risked being captured by the Austrians who had suddenly arrived in the village.

name: Napoleon Monument
description: 4.5 m bronze Statue of Napoleon at Insurgents' Square, formerly Napoleon Square, inaugurated in 2011. Replica of the one erected in 1923.

name: Grave General Mazovskiy - Friedland
description: Commander of the Pavlovsky Grenadier Regiment. He was wounded in combat and taken to a house in the city. When French troops entered the city, he was killed.

name: House Gral Mazovskiy laid wounded - Friedland
description: After the Battle of Friedland, the wounded Russian Major General Nikolai Nikolaevich Mazovsky was taken to this house. When the city was occupied by French troops, the general was bayoneted to death in this very house.

name: Monument to the Victims of the War of 1812 - Berezina
description: Erected in 2002, In 2002 to honor of the fallen at the tragic events of November 1812 during Napoleon's army's crossing of the Berezina River. The approach to the monument is paved with uneven cobblestones, symbolizing the difficult journey each fallen soldier endured on their way to the Berezina.

name: Upper bridge over the Berezina
description: Site where the upper bridge, used by the infantry, was constructed. In 2002 a milestone was erected to replace the destoyed ones built in 1901 at the site discoverd by Ivan Khrisonfonovich Kolodeyev.

name: Artillery bridge over the Berezina
description: Site where the artillery bridge was constructed.(Photo Karavanni zyntek).

name: Monument Battle of Berezina
description: Obelisk erected in 1912 to honor fallen Russian soldiers.

name: French soldiers memorial - Berezina
description: Inaugurated in 1997, it is a tribute to the soldiers of Napoleon's 'Grande Armée' who perished during the catastrophic Battle of Berezina.

name: Memorial chapel - Berezina
description: This memorial is a chapel-monument located dedicated to the fallen at the Battle of Berezina in 1812, one of the most dramatic episodes of the Napoleonic Wars.

name: Milestone - Berezina
description: Memorial erected in 1904 near the turnoff to Studenka on the road from Veselovo to Borisov.

name: Batteries at Borizov
description: The Borisov Batteries (or Zemlyanye Batarei) are a historic site of earthwork fortifications located in Borisov on the banks of the Berezina River to protect the bridgr. Construction began in the spring of 1812 but the invasion of Napoleon's army interrupted the works.

name: History Museum of Borizov
description: The exposition consists of six halls, where the main part is occupied by the events of 1812. On this topic, the museum has a unique collection of artifacts, which is constantly being updated.

name: Mass grave of Russian soldiers - Friedland
description: The mass grave where the fallen at the Battle of Friedland in 1807 were buried.

name: Action of 22 May 1812
location: off the coast of Penmarch, France
description: A small French squadron comprising the French frigates Ariane and Andromaque, and the brig Mameluck returning from a commerce raiding campaign in the Atlantic, met the 74-gun HMS Northumberland while trying the slip to Lorient through the British blockade.

name: Battle of Lyngør
description: Fought on 6 July 1812 between the British and Dano-Norwegian navies as part of the Gunboat War.

name: Battle of Nargö
description: Fought on July 11th 1811 between the Russian cutter Opyt and the British frigate HMS Salsette took place near the northern coast of Estonia by the island of Naissaar (Nargö) in the Baltic Sea, and ended in a British victory.

name: Battlefield of Blaauwberg
description: Also known as the Battle of Cape Town, it was a successful British amphibious operation during the War of the Third Coalition which lasted from 8 to 18 January 1806 and resulted in the capture of the Dutch Cape Colony.

name: Marshal Bernadotte's Birthplace
description: Birthplace and museum of Jean-Baptiste Jules Bernadotte, who became King of Sweden and Norway under the name Charles XIV John.

name: Marshal Poniatowski's Birthplace
description: The palace was commissioned by Count Wirich Philipp von Daun, and construction started in 1713 under the direction of architect Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt. Prince Józef Poniatowski was born in the palace on May 7th 1763.

name: Marshal Kellerman's Birthplace
description: He was born on May 28th 1735 into a Saxon noble family established in Strasbourg.

name: Marshal Kellerman Statue
description: Bronze statue done in 1935 by Léon-Alexandre Blanchot.

name: Marshal Kellerman Tomb
description: The Kellermann family tomb at Père-Lachaise Cemetery at Avenue des Acacias, with mention to the vistories of Valmy and Marengo.

name: Apelstein Nr. 1 Victor - Battle of Wachau
description: Victor, Duke of Beluno II Corps 20,000 men Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 2 original remains - Battle of Wachau
description: Remains of the original milestone placed in a wrong location

name: Liebertwolkwitz Russian-Prussian Monument
description: From here, the 2nd Column under General Prince Eugene of Württemberg opened the Battle of Wachau around 8 a.m. with 10,000 men.

name: Apelstein Nr. 2 Prince Eugene - Battle of Wachau
description: Prince Eugene of Württemberg 10,000 men. Erected in 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Augereau Duke of Castiglione IX Corps 10000 men. Erected in 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Count Lauriston V Corps 15,000 men. Erected in 1861 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Count Lauriston V Corps 15,000 men. Erected in 1861 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Prince Gortschakoff 9000 men. Erected in 1861 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Mac Donald, Duke of Tarentum, XI Corps, 15,000 men. Erected in 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: General Klenau 9th Austrian Corps 24,000 men. Erected in 1861 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 9 Mortier - Battle of Wachau
description: Mortier, Duke of Treviso. 2 divisions of the Young Guard, 12,000 men. Erected in 1861 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Count Pahlen III. 3000 cavalry. Erected in 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 11 Poniatovsky - Battle of Wachau
description: Prince Poniatovsky VIII Corps 8000 men. Erected in 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 12 Bianchi - Battle of Wachau
description: General Bianchi Austrian Reserve. Erected in 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Battlefield of Grijó
description: Fought on May 10th and 11th 1809, iteended in victory for the Anglo-Portuguese Army commanded by Lieutenant-General Sir Arthur Wellesley (the future 1st Duke of Wellington) over the French army commanded by Marshal Nicolas Soult during the Second French invasion of Portugal.

name: Battlefield of Braga
description: The Battle of Braga or Battle of Póvoa de Lanhoso or Battle of Carvalho d'Este (March 20th 1809) saw an Imperial French corps led by Marshal Jean-de-Dieu Soult attack a Portuguese army commanded by Baron Eben

name: Battlefield of Évora
description: An Imperial French division under Louis Henri Loison attacked a combined Portuguese-Spanish force led by Francisco de Paula Leite de Sousa.

name: Apelstein Nr. 13 Oudinot - Battle of Wachau
description: Oudinot, Duke of Reggio, 3rd and 4th Divisions of the Young Guard, 12,000 men. Erected in 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 14 Saint Priest - Battle of Möckern
description: Gen Lieu St. Priest 12000 M. Russians. Erected in 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 15 Compans - Battle of Möckern
description: General Compans 1st Division. Erected in 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 16 Langeron - Battle of Möckern
description: General Count Langeron 18500 M. Russians. Erected in 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 17  Lagrange - Battle of Möckern
description: General Lagrange 2nd Division. Erected in 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Lieutenant General von Sacken 9000 Russians Original: Gen. von Sacken 9000 Cavalry. Erected in 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: General Frederic 3rd Division. Erected in 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Lieutenant General von York 1st Prussian Army Corps 21,000 men.Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: General Dombrowski, General Souham, General Delmas of the III Corps, totaling 12,000 men.Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Memorial crossing Duero River
description: Memorial erected in memory of the battles fought on the banks of the river Douro in 1809.

name: Battlefield of Redinha
description: It was a rearguard action which took place on March 12th 1811, during Masséna's retreat from Portugal as part of the Peninsular War, by a French division under Marshal Ney against a considerably larger Anglo-Portuguese force under Wellington.

name: Memorial El Bodon
description: Memorial erected in 2011 to commemorate the battle on September 25th 1811, between the invading napoleonic army and the anglo-luso coalition.

name: Battlefield of El Bodon
description: It was a rearguard action fought on September 25th 1811 by elements of the Anglo-Portuguese army against waves of French cavalry, supported by a division of infantry of the French army.

name: Apelstein Nr. 22 Gyulai- Battle of Lindenau
description: General Count Gyulai. III. Austrian Corps. 17,000 men. Erected: 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 23 Bertrand- Battle of Lindenau
description: General Count Bertrand, IV Corps, 10,000 men. Erected: 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 24 Frederick VI - Battle of Lindenau
description: Prince of Hesse-Homburg, 1st Colonel of the 3rd Austrian Corps. Erected: 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Monument to Colonel George Lake
description: This monument marks either where he fell or where he was buried by his men after the battle. It was erected by his brother officers as testimony of high regard and esteem.

name: Apelstein Nr. 25 Marmont - Battle of Möckern
description: Marmont Hereditary Duke of Ragusa IV Corps 18000 M. Erected: 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Prince M. Liechtenstein I. Austrian Light Division 5500 M. Erected: 1862 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Mac Donald XI Corps, 12,000 men. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: III. Column General Count Bennigsen 65,000 M. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 29 Marmont - Battle of Schönefeld
description: Marshal Marmont VI Corps 15000 M. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Church of Saint Rocco - Lodi
description: Place where heavy fight between the Austrians and French took place. The image shows as it would be in 1796 with the 'Porta d'Adda' built in 1787.

name: Church of Saint Francis - Lodi
description: From the bell tower of the Church of San Francesco, Napoleon observed and directed the fighting.

name: Scene from the Battle of Lodi
description: Place for the scene of the iconic painting by Felician von Myrbach 'Bonaparte Aiming the Cannon at Lodi'. It depicts Napoleon supervising the position of the French artillery. This action earned him the affectionate nickname 'The Little Corporal' (le petit caporal) from his soldiers.

name: Torre del Puerco
description: Constructed in the XVI century to defend the Spanish coasts from the pirates, it was the testimonial of the Battle of Chiclana between the Anglo-Spanish and French troops and is in the background of the painting by the artist Louis-François Lejeune: Battle of Chiclana.

name: Apelstein Nr. 30 Langeron -Battle of Schoeneufeld
description: Gen. Count LANGERON 30000M. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 31 Lauriston  - Battle of Leipzig
description: Victor Lauriston II and V Corps, 30,000 men. Erected: 1861 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 32 Barclay de Tolly - Battle of Leipzig
description: II. Column General Barclai de Tolly, 50,000 men. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Monarchenhügel (Monarch's Hill)  - Battle of Leipzig
description: The monument commemorates the Battle of Leipzig , where the three allied monarchs observed the course of the battle from here and learned of Napoleon's retreat.

name: Tomb of the Maréchal Guillaume Brune
description: Here rests the Marshal Guillaume Brune, victim of a popular uprising in Avignon in August 1815, as he was returning to France to serve the Emperor in the Hundred Days campaign.

name: Place death of the Maréchal Brune
description: Place where Marshal Brune was killed in August 1815, victim of a popular uprising in Avignon, as he was returning to France to serve the Emperor in the Hundred Days campaign.

name: Birthplace of the Maréchal Brune
description: Maréchal Brune was born on March 13th 1764 at this place.

name: Statue of the Maréchal Brune
description: Statue of Maréchal Brune at his natal town of Brive la Gaillarde. Erected on September 23, 1841, and officially inaugurated on October 3, 1841.

name: Monumento Napoleonico Rivoli Veronesi
description: This monument is dedicated to the memory of the heroes of the Napoleonic era.

name: Statue General Cambronne
description: Bronze statue by Jean-Baptiste Joseph Debay fils erected in 1847.

name: Battlefield of Maloyaroslavets
description: Took place on October 24th 1812. Russian and French armies were evenly matched in the battle and suffered similar casualties, with a marginal edge going to the Franco-Italian army.

name: Battlefield First battle of Polotsk
description: Took place on October 18th 1812. Russian troops under the general command of Bennigsen, acting on instructions from Kutuzov and being part of his army, launched a surprise attack and defeated French troops under Murat's command.

name: Battlefield of Wolkowisk (Volkovysk)
description: Took place from November 14th to the 16th 1812. Austrian, Saxon and French soldiers under Karl Philipp, Prince of Schwarzenberg defeated the Russian army under Fabian Gottlieb von der Osten-Sacken

name: History Museum Bagration
description: The History Museum Bagration in Volkovysk has a collection from the 1812 Russian campaign.

name: Battlefield of Borizov
description: Took place on November 21st 1812, between parts of the French army and parts of the Russian armies. The Russian vanguard under Charles de Lambert eliminated the Franco-Polish force under Dombrowsky.

name: Battlefield of Swolna
description: Took place on August 11th 1812 near the village of Svolna where Oudinot's French ran at the river Svolna into the Russians under d'Auvray.

name: Battlefield of Mir
description: Took place on 9 and 10 July 1812 when three Polish Lancers divisions battled against Russian cavalry, ending in the first major Russian victory in the war.

name: Apelstein Nr. 33 Poniatowski | Augureau | Oudinot - Battle of Leipzig
description: PONIATOWSKI AUGEREAU VIII and IX Corps.OUDINOT III and IV Divisions of the Young Guard, 30,000 men. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Austrian monument 1st Corp - Battle of Leipzig
description: One of four monuments dating from 1913, identical except for their inscriptions, commemorating the successful participation of Austrian troops in the Battle of Leipzig.

name: Austrian monuments 2nd Light Division - Battle of Leipzig
description: One of four monuments dating from 1913, identical except for their inscriptions, commemorating the successful participation of Austrian troops in the Battle of Leipzig.

description: One of four monuments dating from 1913, identical except for their inscriptions, commemorating the successful participation of Austrian troops in the Battle of Leipzig.

name: Austrian monuments 4th Corps - Battle of Leipzig
description: One of four monuments dating from 1913, identical except for their inscriptions, commemorating the successful participation of Austrian troops in the Battle of Leipzig.

description: 1st Colonel, Hereditary Prince of Hesse-Homburg, later General von Nostitz, 50,000 men. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 35 Mortier - Battle of Leipzig
description: Marshal Mortier, 1st and 2nd Divisions of the Young Guard, 10,000 men. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 36 Blücher - Battle of Leipzig
description: V. Colonne Gener. BLUECHER Schles. Army 25000 M. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: General Dombrowski 5000 men. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

description: Bernadotte CARL JOHANN Crown Prince of Sweden 50000 M. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel (photo by: Medien-GbR.de).

name: Apelstein Nr. 39 Reynier - Battle of Leipzig
description: GENERAL REYNIER VII Corps 10,000 men. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 40 Bogue - Battle of Leipzig
description: Captain Bogue English rocket battery. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 41 Ney - Battle of Leipzig
description: Ney Prince of Moscow, left French wing. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 42 Bülow - Battle of Leipzig
description: General BUELOW Count von Dennewitz III Prussian Corps 24,000 men. Erected: 1863 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 43 Friccius - Battle of Leipzig
description: Major Carl Friccius 3rd Königsberg Battalion of the 3rd East Prussian Landwehr Infantry Regiment. Erected: 1864 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 44 Friccius - Battle of Möckern
description: Landwehr from October 15th to 16th, 1813 before the Battle of Möckern. Erected: 1864 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Apelstein Nr. 45 Monarchs - Battle of Leipzig
description: The monarchs receiving the council delegation, October 19, 1813. Erected: 1864 by Dr. Theodor Apel.

name: Siege of Lugo
description: General Nicolas Mahy intended to caputre Lugo defended by French General Fournier who was reinforced on May 22nd 1809 by Soult with 19.000 men. Mahy retreated to Villalba declining to confront a force triple as his 6.000 men.

name: Pałac von Buddenbrock Pielaszkowice (ruins)
description: At this place Napoleon signed the Tripartite Armistice on June 4, 1813.

name: Battle of Talavera - Wellington Command Post
description: Arthur Wellesley's Command Post at 'Cerro Medellín' during the Battle of Talavera.

name: Battle of Talavera - Monument
description: Located south of Cerro de Medellín, one of the key locations of the battle. Its height is 27 meters and it was built between 1989 and 1990 and inaugurated on October 2, 1990.

name: Equestrian statue of Napoleon
description: The equestrian statue depicts Napoleon on horseback and was erected in 1865. It was sculpted in bronze by Gabriel-Vital Dubray.

name: Joseph Bonaparte's house 1815-1816
description: Joseph Bonaparte, king of Naples & Spain lived here, settled here after Napoloen's fall in 1815 and before returning to Europe in 1816.

name: Marengo Museum
description: The Museum intends to tell the story of the Italian campaign of 1800 and the Battle of Marengo by analyzing its causes, developments, and consequences.

name: Birthplace of Marshal Jourdan
description: The house where he was born, April 29th 1762, and spent his childhood is preserved in the town.

name: Birthplace of Marshal Victor
description: Claude Victor Perrin was born at this house on December 7th 1764 in Lamarche. The street got the name in his honour, Duc de Bellune.

name: Birthplace of Marshal Saint-Cyr
description: Historical records note that he was born in a house on Rue de l’Ingressin, near a small stream of the same name. His father was a butcher. Old maps show the Rue de l'Ingressin adjacent to Rue de la Boucherie.

name: Birthplace of Marshal Oudinot
description: Nicolas Charles Oudinot was born in this house on April 25th 1767, Rue de la Couronne, at the intersection with Rue Saint-Antoine, in the lower town (Ville Basse) of Bar-le-Duc.

name: Jean d'Heurs Castle - Oudinot Mansion
description: 18th century castle, was confiscated during the French Revolution and later became the property of the Oudinot family, whose most famous member was Marshal Nicolas Oudinot, Duke of Reggio.

name: Marshal Oudinot Statue
description: Bronze statue sculpted by Jean Debay erected in 1850

name: Marshal Massena family house
description: Masséna spent much of his childhood in his family's ancestral village in a house built in 1722. The stone building is preserved and features a large commemorative plaque with his bust and coat of arms on the facade.

name: Marshal Masséna Statue
description: Sculpted by Albert-Ernest Carrier-Belleuse and inaugurated in 1869, the monument depicts the Niçois-born Napoleonic commander during the Battle of Essling

name: Marshal Masséna Birthplace
description: He was born in Nice on May 6th 1758, and baptised in the cathedral Sainte-Réparate two days later. He was to spend his early childhood to the east of Nice, near Trinité, where Jules had a shop in the hamlet called La Bourgade, was born in the capital of the county on 6 May 1758, and baptised in the cathedral Sainte-Réparate two days later. He was to spend his early childhood to the east of Nice, near Trinité, where Jules had a shop in the hamlet called La Bourgade (where Place Masséna now stands), which was to disappear in 1764.

name: Marshal Soult Birthplace
description: Jean de Dieu Soult was born in this house on March 29th 1769 in Saint-Amans-la-Bastide (today Saint-Amans-Soult). Today it is an appartment building.

name: Marshal Bessières Birthplace
description: The original stone house where Bessières was born on August 6th 1768 to a local surgeon was demolished to make way for a local school facility, known historically as the Collège d'Istrie (named after his title, the Duc d'Istrie).

name: Marshal Suchet Birthplace
description: Historians debate his exact physical birthplace between two specific family properties in Lyon. Some accounts claim he was directly born inside this countryside house, others state it was his family's secondary vacation estate where he spent a significant portion of his childhood.

name: Marshal Suchet official Birthplace
description: The birth certificate states he was born on March 2nd 1770, at his family's urban residence located on Rue Pizay in the center of Lyon.

name: Château de Saint Joseph - Marshal Suchet Mansion
description: On November 16, 1808, Louis Gabriel Suchet married Honorine Anthoine de Saint-Joseph. The château belonged to her father, Antoine-Ignace Anthoine, a wealthy merchant and the Mayor of Marseille. The property became Suchet's seasonal and eventual retirement residence.

name: Marshal Moncey Birthplace
description: Moncey was born on 31 July 1754 in Palise (now part of Moncey), a village in the Franche-Comté region of eastern France.

name: LG William Payne Birthplace
description: He was born at the island of St Christopher in 1759, most probably at Little Sir Gillies Plantation, his father's operation center for his sugar plantation business.

name: LG Rowland Hill Birthplace
description: He was born at his family house on August 11th 1772. The house served as a major seat and residence for the Hill family across multiple generations. The main structure seen today was constructed out of red brick circa 1720 on a 17th century timber-framed building.

name: Apsley House
description: Among a vast art collection, the military elements exhibited at Apsley House comprehensively document the legendary career of Arthur Wellesley, the 1st Duke of Wellington. The collection spans prominent battlefield weapons, political honors, and rare spoils of the Napoleonic Wars-

name: Fili log cabin
description: Place in the village of Fili, just outside Moscow, (nowadays Moscow) where Russian General Mikhail Kutuzov convened a legendary council of war in which was taken the decision to abandon Moscow to the invading French army.

name: Battlefield of Castrejón de Trabancos
description: On July 18th 1812, the French general Marmont failed to complete the maneuver at Castrejón de Trabancos, where the allied rearguard was located and where, during the battle that took place in this town, Wellington almost fell prisoner, the English Lord managing to withdraw all his troops towards the Guareña.

name: Battlefield of Tamames
description: The Battle of Tamames was lost by part of Marshal Michel Ney's French army under General of Division Jean Marchand in the Peninsular War. The French, advancing out of Salamanca, were met and defeated in battle by a Spanish army on 18 October 1809.

name: Battlefield of Sagunto (Sagonte)
description: The Battle of Saguntum (25 October 1811) saw the Imperial French Army of Aragon under Marshal Louis Gabriel Suchet fighting a Spanish army led by Captain General Joaquín Blake. The Spanish attempt to raise the siege of the Sagunto Castle failed when the French, Italians, and Poles drove their troops off the battlefield in rout.

name: Battlefield of María
description: The Battle of María saw a small Spanish army led by Joaquín Blake face an Imperial French corps under Louis Gabriel Suchet.

name: Battlefield of Valls
description: The Battle of Valls was fought on 25 February 1809, during the Peninsular War, between a French force under Laurent Gouvion Saint-Cyr and a Spanish force under Theodor von Reding. Fought near the town of Valls in Catalonia, Spain, the battle ended in a French victory. General Reding was fatally wounded during a cavalry charge against French cavalry.

name: Battlefield of Neresheim
description: The action took place on October 17th 1805. It ended in a victory for the French army commanded by Marshal Joachim Murat. The opposing force was the Austrian army of General Franz von Werneck. The action resulted in the capture of 1,350 men. Among the prisoners was General Rudolf von Sinzendorf. The French also captured 2 colours.

name: Battlefield of Teugen-Hausen (Thann)
description: The battle was fought on 19 April 1809 between the French III Corps led by Marshal Louis-Nicolas Davout and the Austrian III Armeekorps commanded by Prince Friedrich Franz Xaver of Hohenzollern-Hechingen. When the Austrians withdrew that evening, the French won a hard-fought victory over their opponents.

name: Battlefield of Smoliani (Smolyany)
description: The Russians under General Peter Wittgenstein defeated the French forces of Marshal Claude Victor and Marshal Nicholas Oudinot. This battle was the last effort of the French to reestablish their northern flank in Russia, known as the 'Dvina Line'.

name: Battlefield of Epinal
description: The Crown Prince of Württemberg launched a three-column attack against General Rousseau's French forces, who successfully executed an orderly retreat to Charmes despite suffering heavy losses and 500 prisoners due to delayed Allied flank support from General Platoff.

name: Battlefield of Sehested
description: The Battle of Sehested was fought on 10 December 1813 during the Dano-Swedish War of 1813-1814 between a Danish army under Prince Frederik of Hesse and a Coalition force led by Ludwig von Wallmoden-Gimborn.

name: Archduke Charles of Austria Birthplace
description: Archduke Charles was born on September 5th 1771 at the Pitti Palace, residence of his father, Leopold, then Grand Duke of Tuscany.

name: Karl Mack von Leiberich Birthplace
description: He was born on August 25th 1752 in Nennslingen, Principality of Ansbach.

name: Marshal Joseph Radetzky Birthplace
description: He was born on November 2nd 1766 into a noble Bohemian military family of Czech origin at Chateau Třebnice (Trebnitz) near Sedlčany in Bohemia.

name: Karl Philipp, Prince of Schwarzenberg Birthplace
description: He was born on April 18th 1771 at the Palais Schwarzenberg in Vienna, family residence since 1716. In 1987, a scene for the James Bond film 'The Living Daylights' was filmed at the Palais Schwarzenberg.

name: Michael von Melas Birthplace
description: He was born in Radeln, Transylvania, (nowadays Roadeș, part of Bunești commune, Brașov County, Romania) on May 12th 1729 and joined the Austrian Army at age 17.

name: József Alvinczi Birthplace
description: He was born on February 1st 1735 in Alvinc, now part of the village of Vințu de Jos, in the Transylvania region of Romania.

name: Johann I Joseph, Prince of Liechtenstein Birthplace
description: He was born on June 26th 1760 in Vienna, Austria, at the Liechtenstein City Palace which was a family state since 1694.

name: Frederick William, Duke of Brunswick, Birthplace
description: He was born on October 9th 1771 in Braunschweig, Duchy of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, Holy Roman Empire, at the Brunswick Palace.

name: First Battle of Algeciras
description: The First Battle of Algeciras was fought on 6 July 1801 between a Royal Navy squadron and a smaller French Navy squadron lying at anchor in the Spanish port of Algeciras during the Algeciras campaign of the War of the Second Coalition.

name: Second Battle of Algeciras
description: The Second Battle of Algeciras (also known as the Battle of the Gut of Gibraltar) was fought on 12 July 1801 between a Royal Navy squadron and a larger Spanish and French squadron in the Gut of Gibraltar during the Algeciras campaign of the war of the Second Coalition.

name: Battlefield of Tollo
description: The combat of Tollo, also known as the Action of Utiel, took place on August 25, 1812, in Utiel (Valencia). Spanish forces led by General Pedro Villacampa defeated Napoleon's troops under General Maupoint, halting their advance towards Valencia and boosting the morale of the Spanish resistance.

name: Statue de Lasalle au château de Lunéville
description: Bronze equestrian statue of General Lasalle done by Charles Henri Joseph Cordier erected in 1893.

name: Arthur Wellesley, Lord Wellington, Birthplace
description: Still remains uncertainty about both the birthdate and the birthplace of Arthur Wesley, but historinas support the evidence that his family settled into Mornington House, Dublin, at the time of his birth, May 1st 1769.

name: Sir John Moore Birthplace
description: Moore was born on November 13th 1761 in a tenement block called Donald's Land on the north side of the Trongate, east of the Tron Steeple).

name: Sir Thomas Picton Birthplace
description: He was born in Haverfordwest, Pembrokeshire on (probably) 24 August 1758.

name: Sir Thomas Picton Monument
description: The current limestone monument, which is Grade II listed, was erected in 1847, replacing an earlier structure in the town, designed by John Nash, which was weathering badly.

name: Major-General Robert Craufurd Birthplace
description: He was born on May 5th 1764. Some modern biographies suggest he may have been born at Luxborough House in Chigwell, Essex, England. The grand 18th-century estate was demolished around 1800. Today, the site has been completely transformed. The traditional citation is Newark, Ayrshire, Scotland.

name: William Carr Beresford Birthplace
description: Born on October 2nd 1768 as the illegitimate son of the 1st Marquess of Waterford, likely at the family seat Curraghmore House. A specific birth house is unrecorded and some suggested it was in Dublin.

name: General Miguel de Álava Birthplace
description: Born on July 7th 1770 into a noble family of naval tradition, he was the son of Pedro Jacinto de Álava y Navarrete and María Manuela de Esquível y Peralta.

name: General Palafox Birthplace
description: José de Palafox was born in the former palace of his parents (the Marquises of Lazán), located at number 4 Calle de José Palafox, in the Old Town of Zaragoza. At the time of his birth, this street was known as Calle de la Real Aduana (Royal Customs House Street). The building still stands (today it houses the Casa Palacio Palafox Residence) and retains a commemorative plaque on its façade marking the general's birth there on October 28, 1775.

name: Battlefield of Montebello
description: The Battle of Montebello (9 June 1800) was fought near Montebello in Lombardy between a French force under General of Division (GD) Jean Lannes and an Austrian force led by Feldmarschall-Leutnant (FML) Peter Karl Ott von Bátorkéz.

name: Montebello battle memorial
description: Commemorative plaque for the 200th anniversary of the battle placed on the town hall.(image and contribution: D. Timmermans / napoleon-monuments.eu)

name: The Emperor's tree - Boulogne Camp
description: On 30 Messidor year XII (July 19, 1804), Napoleon had lunch at the innkeeper Détaminier's and stopped near an elm tree.(image and contribution: D. Timmermans / napoleon-monuments.eu)

name: Column of the Grande Armée
description: It is a 53 metre high Corinthian order triumphal column (modelled on Trajan's Column and other triumphal columns in Rome). The first stone was put in place by Soult on 18 Brumaire, year 13 (9 October 1804), amidst great festivities and awards of decorations.

name: Légion d'honneur Memorial
description: The Legion of Honour memorial, also called the Legion of Honour stele, is a pyramid-shaped monument recalling the exact position of Napoleon I's throne on August 16, 1804, when the emperor first distributed the Legion of Honour crosses to the soldiers of the Grande Armée at the Boulogne camp.

name: Légion d'honneur Memorial
description: The Legion of Honour memorial, also called the Legion of Honour stele, is a pyramid-shaped monument recalling the exact position of Napoleon I's throne on August 16, 1804, when the emperor first distributed the Legion of Honour crosses to the soldiers of the Grande Armée at the Boulogne camp.

name: Napoleon's barracks
description: During the Boulogne camp, Napoleon's accommodation was located at The Tour d'Ordre (Tower of Order) or Tower of Caligula, a famous ancient Roman lighthouse located in Boulogne-sur-Mer.

name: Artillery park and Navy gunners' camp.
description: Accrodingly to the Map of the Boulogne camp (Boulogne-sur-Mer Municipal Library, No. 36.273.) the artillery magazine and encamptent was located in this area.

name: Napoleon's stone
description: On October 7th 1805 Napoleon Bonaparte observed his troops crossing the Danube River.

name: Napoleon's Fir
description: A historical fir tree planted in 1905 to on a hill overlooking Gottmannshofen to mark the 100th anniversary of the Battle of Wertingen (October 8, 1805)

name: Memorial on Napoleon's Heights
description: Historical accounts suggest that in April 1809, French Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte observed the construction of the Salzach bridge from the hill above, where he delivered his commands. In total, the Emperor's stay in Burghausen lasted five days.

name: Taufkirchen Palais
description: Rebuilt in the Baroque style by J. Anton Graf von Taufkirchen after a fire in 1742, it served as Napoleon's headquarters in April 1809 for a few days.

name: Boulogne Left Encamptment
description: Center of the French troops left encampment from 1803 to 1805. (It run from south to north).

name: Boulogne Right Encamptment
description: Center of the French troops right encampment from 1803 to 1805. (It run from south to north).

name: Napoleon's Quarters at Ranshofen
description: After crossing the Salzach River on April 30th 1809, Napoleon moved into Ranshofen and slept at the castle near the abbey.

name: Napoleon's Quarters at Braunau
description: On May 1, 1809, the Emperor arrived in Braunau and stayed at Josef Schüde's house at Stadtplatz 34, just as he did in 1805.

name: Napoleon's stop at Altheim
description: Local tradition refers this spot as a stop on May 2nd 1809 for Napoleon's 73 km. journey from Braunau to Lambach.

name: Napoleon's stop at Ried
description: Napoleon slept at this place in 1805. There is no evidence but local tradition mention he also stayed in 1809.

name: Napoleon's stop at Lambach
description: Napoleon spent the night at the Benedictine abbey in Lambach on May 2nd 1809 and left Lambach in the morning.

name: Napoleon's Quarters at Ebelsberg
description: On May 3rd 1809, after the battle of Ebelsberg, Napoleon settled at this location.

name: Enns City Tower
description: The almost 60 metre high city tower, built between 1564 and 1568 under Emperor Maximilian II, was used by Napoleon on May 5th 1809 to observe the march of the troops towards Amstetten.

name: Place where Marshal Lannes died
description: Marshal Lannes was mortally wounded by an Austrian cannonball on May 22nd 1809, during the Battle of Aspern-Essling. Following an emergency leg amputation by chief surgeon Dominique-Jean Larrey, he was transported across the Danube to this site, a brewer's house, where he succumbed to gangrene nine days later on May 31st 1809.

name: Schloss Ennsegg
description: Upon the conclusion of the Battle of Ebelsberg (May 3, 1809), Napoleon established his residence at Ennsegg Castle. In 1810, the estate hosted Archduchess Maria Luise and her father, Emperor Franz I, during her journey to visit her husband, Napoleon.

name: Napoleon's obelisk
description: This monument was inaugurated on November 1st 1810 ane is the only remaining trophy in Italy among the many erected in honor of Napoleon.

name: Napoleon's dinner site
description: On May 4th 1805, after reviewing the 26th Line regiment and the Corsican chasseurs at Ebelsberg, Napoleon rode to Enns, had dinner at this site and then slept at the Ennsegg castle.

name: Napoleon's quarters at Sankt Pölten
description: Napoleon departed Melk Abbey on May 8th 1809, and traveled to Sankt Pölten. He stayed for three days at this former Augustinian monastery, which had become the seat of the bishopric in 1785.

name: Melk Abbey
description: On May 7th 1809, after leaving Enns, Napoleon went to the Benedictine abbey of Melk where he spent the night.

name: Napoleon's quarters at Kaiser-Ebersdorf
description: On May 18th 1809, three days before the battle of Aspern-Essling, Napoleon settled into the outbuildings of a brewery close to the Thürnlhof castle.

name: Aspern-Essling 1809 Museum
description: The collection features original weapons, uniforms, ammunition, maps, and personal documents from the soldiers. The Centerpiece is a massive, highly detailed battlefield diorama showcasing 8,500 individually painted figures.

name: Lion of Aspern (Löwe von Aspern)
description: Commissioned in 1858 by sculptor Anton Dominik Fernkorn, the Lion of Aspern (Löwe von Aspern) is a sandstone memorial for the Battle of Aspern-Essling. It portrays a dying lion with a sword tip protruding from beneath its left shoulder blade. The monument serves as a symbol for the massive loss of Austrian lives, despite Austria winning the engagement.

name: French Cemetery Memorial Site
description: A small memorial for the soldiers of the French army who died of typhus in 1809-1810.

name: Jena Stele - Ney
description: Stele marking where Marshal Ney's 6th Corps stood at 11 a.m. at the battle of Jena on October 14th 1806.

name: Auerstedt Stele - Prussian cavalry
description: Stele marking the position of the Prussian cavalry at the battle of Jena on October 14th 1806.

name: Auerstedt Stele - Orange Division
description: Stele marking the position of the Orange Division at the battle of Jena on October 14th 1806.

name: Napoleonic Battery
description: A military defensive structure located in the province of Valencia, built by the Napoleonic army under the command of Suchet. It is a masonry and brick structure built on the bedrock.

name: Marshal Bessieres Memorial
description: On May 1st 1813,on the eve of the Battle of Lützen, a cannonball shattered Bessières' hand and pierced his chest, killing him instantly. This stele points the location of the tragedy.

name: Battle of Jena Remembrance Stone - Marshal Lannes Corp.
description: Marshall Lannes V. Korps 17500 Mann 24 Kanonen

name: Battle of Jena Remembrance Stone - Marshal Lannes Corp.
description: The memorial commemorates the victims of the Battle of Jena, which took place on October 14th 1806.

name: Napoleon's lodging at Łowicz
description: Napoleon stayed at this place on December 18th 1806, on his way to Warsaw after his victories at Jena and Auerstedt.

name: Memorial Napoléon Plage Sud - Fouras
description: Commemorative monument and plaque marking the exact spot on the South Beach (Plage Sud) where Emperor Napoleon departed the French mainland for the last time on July 8th 1815, into permanent exile.

name: Lieutenant-colonel Laurent Drouel memorial
description: Commemorative monument of the Drouel family. Laurent Drouel was a lieutenant-colonel and officer of the Legion of Honor, fought under Napoleon in Italy and Russia, where he was seriously wounded in 1812. Charles and Victor also served: one died on the field of honor in Russia, the other was decorated as a Knight of Saint Louis and of the Legion of Honor.

name: Battlefield of Zornoza
description: It was one of the opening engagements in Napoleon's invasion of Spain. The battle was intended to encircle and crush the left wing of the Spanish front. The Spanish infantry was swiftly thrown back but escaped in good order.

name: Battlefield of Valmaseda (Balmaseda)
description: During Lieutenant-General Blake's retreat from superior French armies in northern Spain. Reinforced by veteran regular infantry from General La Romana's Division of the North (Spanish: Division del Norte), Blake's force suddenly turned on its pursuers and ambushed Marshal Victor's errant vanguard under Général de division Villatte.

name: Fist battle of Castalla battlefield
description: A small Spanish army commanded by Joseph O'Donnell advanced to attack an Imperial French division under the leadership of Jean Isidore Harispe.

name: Second battle of Castalla battlefield
description: An Anglo-Spanish-Sicilian force commanded by Lieutenant General Sir John Murray fought Marshal Louis Gabriel Suchet's French Army of Valencia and Aragon. Murray's troops successfully repelled a series of French attacks on their hilltop position, causing Suchet's III corps to retreat.

name: Austerlitz Horse Memorial
description: This is a tribute to the thousands of horses killed at the battlefield of Austerlitz. This 300-kilogram statue of a rearing horse after being shot was created by sculptor Nikos Armutidis.

name: Cairn of Peace Memorial - Austerlitz
description: It is the first peace memorial in Europe. It was dedicated in 1923 to honor the men fallen at the Battle of Austerlitz,

name: Battlefield of Roncesvalles
description: It took place at the high Roncevaux Pass between French and Anglo-Portuguese forces on July 25th 1813. The French emerged victorious by assaulting this mountain pass.

name: Battlefield of La Suffel (Strasburg)
description: It was fought on June 28th 1815 and was a French victory over Austrian forces and the last French pitched battle victory in the Napoleonic Wars.

name: Battlefield of Loriol
description: On April 2nd 1815, two days after the Battle of Montélimar, the Duke of Angoulême decided to fight a small Bonapartist force defending Valence across the Drôme River.

name: Battlefield of Kalisz
description: On February 13th 1813 Russian forces under General Ferdinand von Wintzingerode caught and defeated General Jean Reynier's retreating Franco-Saxon VII Corps. The victory forced Reynier to withdraw into Saxony and separated a Saxon brigade that joined Prince Poniatowski's Polish Army.

name: Battle of Kalisz Memorial
description: This memorial stone commemorating the Battle of Kalisz. It was originally erected in 1985 on the border of the villages of Kokanin and Niedźwiady and underwent a major restoration by the local municipality in 2016 to improve the clearing and fencing around it.

name: Barracks Duchy of Warsaw 8th Inf. Reg.
description: Associated in local tradition with the 8th Infantry Regiment of the Duchy of Warsaw, commanded by poet Cyprian Godebski, who died at the Battle of Raszyn in 1809.

name: Napoleonic obelisk
description: It was erected in 1813 at the burial site of Napoleonic soldiers who died in the field hospital from exhaustion, disease, and frostbite. Their number is estimated at between 300 and 1,200.

name: Battlefield of Altenzaun
description: Retreating from Jena, Ludwig von Yorck's rearguard established a strong defensive line along the Elbe River,near Altenzaun, to protect the crossing. French infantry tried to outflank them but he was able to stop them allowing the remaining Prussian troops to cross the Elbe safely.

name: Battlefield of Zehdenick
description: The Prussian light cavalry, commanded by Generalmajor Schimmelpfennig, charged home against Lasalle's hussars and were holding their own until Grouchy's dragoons arrived.

name: Battlefield of Amstetten
description: It was a minor engagement occurred on November 5th 1805, when the retreating Russo-Austrian troops, led by Mikhail Kutuzov, were intercepted by Marshal Joachim Murat's cavalry and a portion of Marshal Jean Lannes' corps.

name: Lubomirski Palace
description: It was in this palace that Prince Józef Poniatowski had his headquarters before the beginning of the Galician campaign against the Austrians in 1809.

name: Battlefield of Wrzawy
description: On June 12th 1809 the forces of the Duchy of Warsaw, led by Prince Józef Antoni Poniatowski, clashed against the Austrian Imperial army under the command of Archduke Ferdinand Karl Joseph of Austria.

name: Battlefield of Hof
description: On February 6th 1807, a military rearguard action between Napoleon Bonaparte's French Grand Army and the Imperial Russian Army took place just one day before the bloody and inconclusive Battle of Eylau.

name: Général Darricau house
description: By an imperial decree on January 23rd 1806, the historic Bishop's Palace of Dax was allocated to General-Senator Augustin Darricau as his official private residence. He died of illness here in 1819

name: Battlefield of Rovereto
description: On September 4th 1796 a French army commanded by Napoleon Bonaparte defeated an Austrian corps led by Paul Davidovich. The battle was fought near the town of Rovereto, in the upper Adige River valley in northern Italy.

name: Battlefield of Peschiera
description: The Battle of Peschiera was a minor clash that occurred on August 6th 1796 between the Austrian troops of General Anton Lipthay and the French division of General André Masséna.

name: Szydłowiec Castle
description: On July 6th 1809, on their way from Warsaw to Krakow, the Duchy of Warsaw army corps under the command of Generals Jan Henryk Dąbrowski, Józef Zajączek, Aleksander Rożniecki, and Michał Sokolnicki converged on Szydłowiec. Prince Józef was quartered and spent the night in Szydłowiec Castle.

name: Monument to the Drum of Arcole
description: Sculpted by Jean Barnabé Amy it was erected in 1894 in honor of André Estienne, a drummer in the Army of Italy commanded by General Bonaparte, who was born in this town in 1777.

name: Combat of Pfaffenhoffen
description: On April 19th 1809, the advanced troops of Marshal Oudinet reached Pfaffenhoffen where they clashed with a small detachment of Hiller's Austrian VI Corps under Major Karl von Scheibler.

name: Siege of Almeida (1810)
description: In the siege of Almeida, Portugal, the French corps of Marshal Michel Ney captured the border fortress from Brigadier General William Cox's Portuguese garrison.

name: Blockade of Almeida (1811)
description: In the Blockade of Almeida (14 April – 10 May 1811) the French garrison under Antoine François Brenier de Montmorand was surrounded by approximately 13,000 Anglo-Allied soldiers led by Generals Sir Alexander Campbell, 1st Baronet and Sir William Erskine, 2nd Baronet.

name: Battlefield of Montenotte
description: Fought on April 12th 1796 between the French army under General Napoleon Bonaparte and an Austrian corps under Count Eugène-Guillaume Argenteau.

name: Battlefield of Panaro
description: On April 3dr 1815 King Joachim Murat's Neapolitan forces defeated a smaller Austrian force under Frederick Bianchi early in the Neapolitan War. This defeat on the banks on the Panaro River, just south of Modena forced the Austrians to retreat behind the Po River.

name: Battlefield of Millesimo
description: The Battle of Millesimo, fought on 13 and 14 April 1796, was the name that Napoleon Bonaparte gave in his correspondence to one of a series of small battles that were fought in Liguria, Northern Italy.

name: Château de Marracq ruins
description: In 1808, the abdication of the Bourbons of Spain in favour of Neopleon I was signed in the Castle of Marracq. Then Napoleon installed his brother Joseph Bonaparte on the throne of Spain.

name: Château de Joux
description: Ordered by Napoloen, the leader of the Haitian Revolution, Toussaint Louverture, was imprissoned here where he died on April 7th 1803.

name: Napoleon crossing the Alps
description: It depicts Napoleon realistically—wearing a simple greatcoat and riding a mule—honoring the genuine grit, logistical feat, and local mountain expertise required to move 40,000 troops through the unnavigable pass.

name: Primacial Palace
description: The palace and its most famous chamber, the Hall of Mirrors, were the location of the signing of the fourth Peace of Pressburg by Johann I Josef, Prince of Liechtenstein, Ignácz Gyulay and Charles Maurice de Talleyrand in 1805 after the Battle of Austerlitz, which effectively ended the War of the Third Coalition.

name: Moravian Sun Inn
description: Joseph Bonaparte stayed at the inn in the summer of 1821 and coincided precisely with the summer he received news of Napoleon's death. A year prior to his visit a devastating fire destroyed his residence in New Jersey. While rebuilding his opulent French-style estate, Joseph frequently traveled the region, finding the peaceful community of Bethlehem an ideal place to rest.

name: Point Breeze Estate Mansion
description: It was the home of Joseph Bonaparte from 1816 to 1839. At the time of the first mansion's construction in 1819, it was the largest residence in the United States. It was torn down in the 1850's

name: Lansdowne Mansion
description: Joseph Bonaparte he rented this grand, historic mansion to the west of the city from the Penn family before settling permanently at Point Breeze. The mansion tragically burned down in 1854.

name: Natural Bridge Joseph Bonaparte's House
location: Natural Bridge, Jefferson County, New York
description: Joseph Bonaparte bought a large timber barn like house to a man named Bingham and had finished by 1828. It stood where is now Main St.and it was part of th 118.000 acres he owned at Jefferson County.

name: Point Breeze Estate Gardens
description: :This is the only remaining building of Joseph Bonaparte's estate. He was an avid landscape architect who shaped Point Breeze into one of America's first intentionally designed picturesque country estates.

name: Point Breeze Estate
description: :This landscape painting attributed to Charles B. Lawrence, titled 'Point Breeze, the Estate of Joseph Napoleon Bonaparte at Bordentown, New Jersey' is exhibited at the Art Institute of Chicago.

name: Lake Bonaparte
description: The lake was part of the 150260 acres land Joseph Bonaparte bought from James Le Ray de Chaumont in 1818.  Because the lake had not yet been officially charted, Bonaparte's designation of 'Lake of Diana' (and later 'Lake Diana') serves as its first documented name in historical records.

name: Le Presbytère
description: Napoleon stayed at this house (then serving as the town's sub-prefecture) for a single night, from June 13 to June 14, 1815. This brief stopover took place during the opening days of the Hundred Days Campaign, just as the French army was concentrating near the border before launching its invasion of Belgium.

name: Leiden gunpowder disaster
description: Occurred on January 12th 1807 when a ship carrying hundreds of barrels of black powder exploded in the Dutch town of Leiden. This catastrophic event resulted in 151 fatalities and the destruction of over 200 buildings.

name: Poznań Former Jesuit College
description: Napoleon used the building of the Jesuit College as his residence during his stays in the city in 1806, 1807, and 1812.

name: 1813 Memorial Stone
description: This  memorial stone was erected in 1913 under a massive oak tree (a natural monument) in the village center to commemorate the successful battles against Napoleon, including the Battle of Leipzig in 1813.

name: Jean-Andoche Junot Birthplace
description: He was born into a bourgeois family in Bussy-le-Grand, Burgundy, on September 25th 1771.

name: Napoleon's house in Nice
description: A 24-year-old Napoleon, newly promoted to Brigadier General and Commander of the Artillery for the Army of Italy, live in this house while inspecting coastal defenses from Marseille to Menton and plan an invasion strategy.

name: Battlefield of Langenau
description: On October 16, 1805, French 1st Hussars under Jacques Tilly halted a bogged-down Austrian advance led by Prince Friedrich von Hohenzollern at Langenau.

name: General Henryk Dąbrowski's Birthplace
description: The mound is placed where once stood the house were General Jan Henryk Dąbrowski was born on August 2nd 1755. It was built by soldiers of the Polish army using soil brought from various historical battlefields and places where the general resided.

name: General Henryk Dąbrowski Monument
description: The sandstone monument was placed in the village in 1872. It was created by Kraków stonemason Edward Stehlik and was erected as part of the celebrations of the 75th anniversary of the founding of the Polish Legions.

name: Battle of Leipzig commemorating plaque
description: The plaque was installed in 1913 to mark the 100th anniversary of the Battle of Leipzig (1813). At the time, the village of Gorzeszów was named Görtelsdorf and belonged to the Kingdom of Prussia within the German Empire.

name: Vistula Legion plaque
description: The plaque in Legnica was placed to commemorate a historical military stopover made by Polish Uhlans (lancers) on May 14th 1807, on their way 'from Italian land to Poland'

name: Battlefield of Herbrechtingen
description: This clash on October 15th 1805, was a sharp cavalry action where Marshal Joachim Murat's French cavalry pursued some of the retreating Austrian corps under General Major Zinzendorf command.

name: Norman Cross Prison
description: Norman Cross Prison was established in 1797 as the world's first purpose-built prisoner-of-war camp, housing up to 10,000 mostly French inmates during the Napoleonic Wars.

name: Norman Cross Prison Memorial
description: The memorial to the 1,770 prisoners who died at Norman Cross was erected in 1914 by the Entente Cordiale Society beside the Great North Road.

name: Battlefield of Nordlingen
description: On October 17th 1805 Murat commanding the Reserve cavalry pursued twelve retreating Austrian corps cavalry squadrons commanded by Karl Philipp, Prince of Schwarzenberg.

name: Capitulation at Trochtelfingen
description: On October 18th 1805 French forces under Marshal Joachim Murat forced retreating Austrian troops under General Franz von Werneck to surrender roughly 8,000 to 15,000 men.

name: Veste Oberhaus
description: During his campaign against Austria, Napoleon used the fortress as a border outpost under the control of his Bavarian allies, though it ultimately surrendered to the Austrian army on October 25th 1805.

name: Battlefield of Lambach (Ulm Campaign)
description: On October 31st 1805, the French vanguard of Marshal Davout's III Corps achieved a minor victory by defeating a retreating Austro-Russian rearguard under Prince Bagration and General Schustekh during a series of sharp actions at Haag and Lambach.

name: Strub Pass clash
description: On November 2nd & 3rd 1805, Austrian forces and Tyrolean militia successfully defended key passes to protect withdrawing troops from a Bavarian advance.

name: Veste Oberhaus
description: The monument honors the Tyrolean and local defenders (Landesverteidiger) who fought bravely in the battles fought at this strategic pass during the Napoleonic Wars in 1800, 1805, and 1809.

name: Steyer clash
description: Maximilian, Count of Merveldt was retreating his six battalion Reserve Corp through the mountains when on November 4th he was chased and defeated by Caffarelli's division at Steyer. This was the end of Merveldt's forces as a fighting division.

name: Scharnitz clash site (ruins)
description: It took place on November 4 and 9, 1805, when Franco-Bavarian forces attacked and were repulsed at the strategic Porta Claudia mountain fortification guarding the Scharnitz Pass on the border of Bavaria and Tyrol. (Image source: Frieda Bauer: Military History Series Issue 60).

name: Leutasch clash site (ruins)
description: On November 4 1805, Ney was able to overrun the fortified pass of Leutasch opening the road to Innsbruck. (Image source: Frieda Bauer: Military History Series Issue 60).

name: The Battle of Scharnitz for the Porta Claudia Fortress
description: The painting by Mathias Noder, housed in the German Historical Museum, depicts the French forces under Marshal Michel Ney, guided by Bavarian allies, bypassed the strategically fortified mountain pass of Porta Claudia to ambush the Austrian garrison on November 4th 1805.

name: San Pietro in Gu action
description: Archduke Charles retreated from the battlefield of Caldiero when the French forces commanded by General Molitor raached his rearguard commanded by General Frimont at San Pietro in Gu on November 4th. One battalion of the Kreutzer Grenz Infantry Regiment Nr. 5 was destroyed.

name: Burning of English Merchandise
description: Painted in 1810 by Johann Carl Wilck, 'Burning of English Merchandise on the Fischerfeld near Frankfurt am Main' is on display at the Historical Museum of Frankfurt. The artwork depicts the public burning of smuggled goods, which served as a dramatic demonstration to enforce compliance with Napoleon's Continental Blockade and the Berlin Decree.

name: Clash at Weyer
description: The engagement at Weyer on November 7th 1805, was a small but successful military action where Marshal Auguste Marmont’s French II Corps overtook and captured two battalions of Austrian troops under Count Maximilian von Merveldt.

name: Commemorative plaque Battle of Lübeck
description: A bronze memorial relief at the Burgtor commemorates this battle. It depicts the mounted troops with drawn weapons. The plaque was designed by Walter Jahn, presumably in the 1950s, possibly to mark the 150th anniversary of the battle in 1956.

name: Burgator (Castle gates) of Lübeck
description: The Burgtor (Castle Gate) served as the crucial northern defense point and main theater of combat during the Battle of Lübeck on November 6, 1806.

name: Bertrand Museum
description: Musée Bertrand in Châteauroux, France, features intimate personal artifacts, campaign equipment, and memorabilia from Napoleon Bonaparte and his loyal Grand Marshal, General Henri-Gatien Bertrand, who followed the emperor into exile on Saint Helena.

name: Combat at Mariazell
description: This action on November 8th 1805, resulted in a decisive French victory when Marshal Davout's vanguard intercepted and destroyed an Austrian corps retreating through the mountains of Styria. This clash cleared a direct path for Napoleon to capture Vienna.

name: Combat of Valvasone
description: A minor rearguard action was fought at Valvasone, near the Tagliamento River, on November 11th 1805, where Austrian forces under Archduke Charles successfully fended off pursuing French cavalry during their retreat.

name: Capitulation of Dornbirn
description: The Austrain forces commanded by Feldmarschall-Leutnant Franz Jellacic were isolated near Lake Constance  by superior numbers of French troops under Marshal Pierre Augereau. On November 13th 1805 Jellacic surrendered the infantry and artillery under his command. However, his cavalry managed to escape to Bohemia.

name: Battlefield of Schöngrabern
description: It was a critical rearguard action fought on November 16th 1805. The battle resulted in a tactical French victory but a strategic success for the Russian Empire, as a vastly outnumbered Russian rearguard successfully delayed Napoleon's forces. This delay provided enough time for the main Allied armies to safely unite before the decisive Battle of Austerlitz.

name: General Rowland Hill Birthplace
description: Hill was born on 11 August 1772 in Prees, Shropshire. He was the second son and fourth child of Sir John Hill. He served under Sir John Moore and under Wellington during the Peninsular War.

name: Napoleon House - Louisiana
description: Located in the heart of the French Quarter, the historic Napoleon House dates back to 1794. It got its name from a fascinating local legend: the home was supposedly prepared as a safe haven for Napoleon Bonaparte after his exile but his death in 1821 put an end to the plan.

name: Combat of Gradisca
description: On November 16th 1805, Austrian forces under Karl von Vincent successfully held off an attempt by French general Claude-Prieur Molitor's forces to cross the Isonzo River at Gradisca d'Isonzo, as Archduke Charles's Austrian army retreated eastward.

name: Museum of Military History of Artillery
description: The Museum houses an important section dedicated to the Patriotic War of 1812 and the Napoleonic Wars, highlighting war trophies, the emperor's personal weapons and French artillery pieces from that era.

name: Battle for Moscow 7 September 1812
description: Painted by German military artist Albrecht Adam in 1825, 'Battle for Moscow 7 September 1812' is a Romantic-era historical artwork that captures the harsh realities of the Battle of Borodino. Now preserved in the State Hermitage Museum, this oil and gouache work on paper offers a rare, first-hand account of Napoleon's invasion of Russia.

name: Battle of Kliastitsy
description: Battle of Kliastitsy, oil on canvas done in 1856 by Peter von Hess, depicts the fierce between Russian troops and the French. The painting captures the intensity of the battle.

name: Jacinto Ruiz Statue
description: It is the work of the sculptor Mariano Benlliure and was inaugurated in 1891 in homage to Lieutenant Jacinto Ruiz y Mendoza, one of the leaders of the resistance of the Monteleón Artillery Park during the uprising of May 2, 1808 in Madrid.

name: Maison Giubega
description: This 15th-century palace served as the Calvi residence for the Bishops of Sagone and later belonged to Laurent Giubega, the godfather of Napoleon Bonaparte. Napoleon famously took refuge here in 1793 when his family fled Ajaccio.

name: Tomb of General Dorsenne
description: Jean-Marie Dorsenne began his career as a volunteer in 1791 and rose to the rank of Major General in 1809. He died in 1812 from wounds sustained at the Battle of Essling. His name is inscribed on the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.

name: Tomb of General Clarke
description: Henri Jacques Guillaume Clarke  was a French military officer, diplomat, and politician of Irish origin who served as Minister of War of the First French Empire from 1807 to 1814. Financial difficulties delayed the construction of the monument until five years after the Marshal's burial. Designed by Paul Thomas Bartholomé, architect of the Hôtel des Invalides, the structure was transported from Paris to Neuwiller by a team of 24 horses and installed during the summer of 1823.

name: Marshal Ney's tomb
description: Marshal Ney's burial place is one of the most moving sites in Père Lachaise Cemetery. Located in division 29, the grave is marked by a simple, powerful monument featuring a broken sword, symbolizing his execution. This spot is a pilgrimage site for those who admire Ney's courage and tragic end.

name: Joachim Murat's memorial
description: Murat's family grave is a memorial to the Marshal. Murat is not actually buried at Pere-Lachaise and the location of his body is unknown after his execution.

name: Marshal Suchet's tomb
description: Marshal Suchet's tomb is a significant landmark in Père Lachaise Cemetery, located in division 39.

name: Marshal Grouchy's tomb
description: Unlike Napoleon's top commanders—like Ney, Davout, and Masséna—who rest together in the cemetery's famous 'Marshals' Corner,' Grouchy's tomb sits isolated in a distant eastern section.
