This physical separation mirrors his historical legacy, as he was famously blamed for the French defeat at Waterloo and branded an outcast.

name: Marshal Victor's tomb
description: Located in the 17th Division of Paris's famous Père Lachaise Cemetery, the tomb of Marshal Claude-Victor Perrin (the Duke of Belluno) stands as a dignified, traditional military monument.

name: Marshal Gouvion Saint-Cyr's tomb
description: Standing as one of the most majestic military monuments in Paris's historic Père Lachaise Cemetery, the tomb honors Laurent de Gouvion Saint-Cyr, Marquis and Marshal of France. Designed by architect Louis Visconti, the imposing monument is topped with a life-sized white marble statue of the Marshal standing upright on a tall, rectangular pedestal. Carved by sculptor Pierre-Jean David d'Angers in 1833, the figure holds a strategic battle plan in one hand.

name: General Étienne de Nansouty's tomb
description: He served as the First Inspector General of the Cavalry of the Imperial Guard and famously commanded the Guard's elite heavy cavalry squadrons during the grueling 1812 Russian Campaign and the 1814 Defensive Campaign in France.

name: Marechal Augereau's tomb
description: Marechal Pierre François Charles Augereau, Duke of Castiglione, is buried in a humble Family Burial chapel.

name: Dode de la Brunerie's tomb
description: Guillaume Dode, is buried in a Family Burial chapel. He served in Egypt, Spain and Russia.

name: Auguste Marie & Augustin Gabriel Aboville tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 25, chemin Laplace 3rd line), Paris
description: Both brothers were artillery officers. Two standing cannons flank the tomb. Auguste Marie d'Aboville was a French artillery officer, Commander of the Horse Artillery of the Imperial Guard, rose to the rank of general of brigade. Augustin Gabriel, the older brother of Augustin-Marie, rose to the rank of Brigadier General and served in Spain.

name: Marshal Davout's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 28, chemin Masséna 2nd line), Paris
description: Auguste Marie d'Aboville was a French artillery officer, Commander of the Horse Artillery of the Imperial Guard, rose to the rank of general of brigade.

name: Guillaume François d'Aigremont's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 53, avenue de la Chapelle 2nd line), Paris
description: He was a French general de brigade who fought at the Battle of Marengo in 1800 and the Battle of Maria in Spain during the Peninsular War. He was made a baron during the First French Empire by Napoleon Bonaparte. He was an officer of the Legion of Honour and a knight of the Order of Saint Louis.

name: General Foy's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 28, chemin Saint-Louis, 1ère ligne, M=R-31), Paris
description: Maximilien-Sébastien Foy, was a French general who served in Spain and Portugal. During the Peninsular War, Foy distinguished himself in numerous battles and campaigns, earning a reputation for bravery, leadership, and tactical skill. He was wounded several times but continued to serve with distinction.

name: General Jean Baptiste Gauldrée Boilleau's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 01, avenue Principale, 5ème ligne, M=AJ-16), Paris
description: From 1806 to 1815, Gauldrée-Boilleau fought in all of Napoleon's campaigns across Italy, Portugal, Russia, Germany, and France. He served as aide-de-camp in Catalonia, organized logistics in Magdeburg, and later became Marshal Macdonald's chief aide-de-camp during the final campaigns of 1813 and 1814.

name: General François Joseph Gérard's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 38, chemin Masséna, 1ère ligne, M=L-32), Paris
description: François Joseph Gérard, served as Colonel of Hussards in 1806 and raised to General de Brigade in 1809 and General de Division in 1813.

name: Manuel Godoy's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 45, avenue Transversale n°1 ; 3ème ligne, M=O-19), Paris
description: Manuel Godoy, was a Spanish statesman who was the private secretary to King Charles IV of Spain from 1792 to 1798, and Prime Minister from 1798 to 1808. He was a key figure in the history of Spain during the Peninsular War, serving as a minister to King Charles IV of Spain during the French invasion of Spain in 1808.

name: Charles-Étienne Gudin's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 40, chemin des Anglais, 1ère ligne, M=M-29, carditaphe), Paris
description: A schoolmate of Napoleon at the military school of Brienne-le-Château, he was promoted to general of division in 1800.Gudin was widely regarded as one of the most capable officers in the Grande Armée and distinguished himself at the battles of Auerstaedt, Eylau, Eckmühl and Wagram, where he demonstrated his talents as a tactician. He was mortally wounded at the Battle of Valutino during the Russian campaign on 19 August 1812.

name: Charles-Étienne Gudin's Birthplace
description: Gudin was born into a noble family in Montargis on 13 February 1768. He was the son of Gabriel Louis Gudin, an officer of the Artois Regiment. studied at the École de Brienne at the same time as Napoleon Bonaparte.

name: Marshal McDonald's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 37, avenue des Acacias, 1ère ligne, M=Q-34), Paris
description: Marshal McDonald served with distinction in the French revolutionary armies and later in the Napoleonic army, earning promotion to Marshal of the Empire in 1809. He participated in numerous campaigns and battles, demonstrating bravery and tactical skill. He is burried in a Family vault.

name: Marshal François Joseph Lefèbvre's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 28, chemin Camille Jordan, 1ère ligne), Paris
description: He began his career under the Ancien Régime as a sergeant in the elite French Guards, making him one of the few marshals to rise entirely from the enlisted ranks through sheer grit and bravery.The decoration of the beautiful marble monument is the work of Pierre Jean David d'Angers.

name: Marshal André Masséna's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 28, chemin Masséna, 1ère ligne, M=O-33), Paris
description: A marble obelisk adorned with a profile of Masséna by François Joseph Bosio and his coat of arms (with the angel of victory), from which hang two medals, under a crown and on a garland held by two swords honors him at his tomb.

name: Marshal Jean Sérurier's memorial
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 39, chemin Masséna, 1ère ligne, M=N-33, cénotaphe), Paris
description: Sérurier died of illness on December 21, 1819. His body has rested at Les Invalides since 1847. A simple stone cenotaph is in Père Lachaise Cemetery.

name: Marshal Édouard Mortier's memorial
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 28, chemin Camille Jordan, 10ème ligne, M=P-32, carditaphe), Paris
description: This is Marshal Mortier's family grave. He is burried at les Invalides, but his heart it is burried in here as a plaque on the left hand side of the rear wall describes.

name: Marshal Dominique Pérignon's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 24, chemin Laplace, 1ère ligne, M=P-20), Paris
description: The monument is the unsigned work of architect Etienne Hippolyte Godde, the designer of the Père Lachaise chapel, and the sculpture, also unsigned, is by Jean Baptiste Plantar. The inscriptions are now illegible.

name: Marie Walewska's carditaphe
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 67, chemin d'Ornano, 1ère ligne), Paris
description: The Family d'Ornano vault contains the heart of Marie Walewska,her body was returned to Poland where she rests in the church of Kiernozia.

name: Alexandre Colonna, comte Walewski's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 66, avenue Circulaire, 1ère ligne), Paris
description: Alexandre Colonna-Walewski was the son of Napoleon I and comtesse Maria Walewska, «l'épouse polonaise de Napoléon».

name: Marie Walewska's tomb
description: Saint Margaret's Church in Kiernozia is a historic, brick-built Roman Catholic parish church located in Kiernozia, Poland, famous for holding the family crypt and remains of Marie Walewska.

name: Mauzoleum Rodziny Yorck von Wartenburg
description: The Yorck-Wartenburg family mausoleum is an early 19th-century Neoclassical building designed by architect Carl Gotthard Langhans. It served as the resting place for members of the distinguished Prussian family, including Field Marshal Ludwig Yorck von Wartenburg.

name: General Maurice d'Albignac's tomb,
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 23, avenue Transversale n° 1, 5ème ligne, M=P-18), Paris
description: Maurice François (de Rivet) d'Albignac (1777-1824), General and commander of the Guard in 1813, has a modest tombstone in Père Lachaise.

name: General Pierre Alexandre Allent's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 10, chemin du Père Eternel, 1ère ligne, M=AB-19), Paris
description: He was a major in the Corps of Engineers, director of the fortifications depot, and then chief of staff of the Paris National Guard. He was promoted to brigadier general in 1813 and then to lieutenant general in 1814.

name: General Alexandre d'Alton's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 25, chemin Molière et La Fontaine, 1ère ligne, M=Q-22), Paris
description: Grand officer of the Legion d'Honneur he was a veteran of Marengo, Austerlitz and Russia.

name: Colonel François Anthoine's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 35, avenue des Acacias, 6ème ligne), Paris
description: Joined the army in 1804 as a volunteer in the 1st Dragoon Regiment. Served in Spain as captain of Hussards, he rose to Colonel in 1814.

name: General Jacques Philippe Avice's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 38, chemin Masséna, 1ère ligne), Paris
description: He rapidly rose through the cavalry ranks, becoming  brigade commander in the 11th Hussars in 1793. After fighting in the Italian campaign, he went on to serve as colonel of the 29th Dragoons before ultimately achieving the rank of brigadier general in command of the 6th Lancers.

name: Captain Coignet Birthplace
description: He was born on August 16th 1776 and joined the army in 1799. Veteran of all the campaigns he rose to the rank of Captain of the Imperial Guard.

name: Captain Coignet tomb
description: Captain Jean-Roch Coignet died on December 10th 1865, after a long military career in the Imperial Guard during the Napoleonic Wars and later becoming famous for his memoirs.

name: Captain Coignet home
description: Captain Jean-Roch Coignet Coignet settled in Auxerre where we wrote his memoirs after his wife death.

name: General Dominique Vandamme tomb
description: General Dominique Vandamme died on July 15th 1830. He is burried at his birth town. A central commemorative stone column displays a comprehensive list of his famous military campaigns and historic Napoleonic battles.

name: Commemorative stele General Vandamme
description: Erected on June 25th 1922, to honor General Vandamme, it lists his most famous military campaigns, including the battles of Hondschoote, Ulm, Austerlitz, and Fleurus.

name: Château Vandamme
description: Also known as La Frégate. The property was purchased in 1794 by General Vandamme, who remodeled the structure in 1810 to resemble a military warship complete with rounded ends and porthole windows.

name: General François Durutte's Tomb
description: A true warrior who fought up to Waterloo, General Durutte retired to his wife's family estate near Ypres after Napoleon's fall. Following his death on April 18, 1827, he was buried there in a neoclassical tomb, which remains the oldest in the city's municipal cemetery.

name: Martin Le Graverand's Tomb
description: He was a native of Ypres, born on May 20, 1775.He made a career in the National Guard, had the opportunity to transfer to the Imperial Guard. In 1814 returned to Ypres where he died in 1862.

name: Lt. Colonel Philippe de Coenens's Tomb
description: Born on October 25, 1793, in Bouvignes-sur-Meuse. He began a military career, fought in the battles of Lutzen, Bautzen, and Wurschen, and was wounded and taken prisoner in 1813. Died in 1850 at the age of 57 as a retired lieutenant colonel

name: Captain Lambert Joseph de Stuers's Tomb
description: Born in Holland, De Stuers joined Napoleon's Grande Armée and served Captain in the Grenadiers of the Dutch Guard, then in the 2nd Foot Grenadiers of the Old Guard. As a battalion commander he participated in the Russian campaign. Despite being wounded in Russia, he survived and fought alongside Napoleon until his final defeat at Waterloo. He died in 1866 and was buried in the family tomb.

name: Yper Museum
description: There was a flourishing and active 'Association of Former Comrades-in-Arms of the French Empire' in the city, and the Ypres Museum possesses several beautiful porcelain cards from this veterans' association.

name: Skirmish at Flitscher-Klause
description: Two Austrian battalions under command of General Major Siegenthal stop the advance of Brigade General Lacour's four dragoon regiments on November 19th 1805.

name: Musée de la Légion d'honneur
description: Since 1804, this building has been called the Palais de la Légion d'Honneur, and it is the seat of France's highest honours: the Légion d'honneur (1802).

name: General Tuckov's stand at Valutin hill
description: General-major Pyotr Tuckov held this crucial position from morning until late afternoon. Despite being surrounded and repeatedly wounded, he and his men never retreated, preventing a breakthrough that could have led to the envelopment of the entire Russian army.

name: General Tuckov's stand at Valutin hill
description: General-major Pyotr Tuckov held this crucial position from morning until late afternoon. Despite being surrounded and repeatedly wounded, he and his men never retreated, preventing a breakthrough that could have led to the envelopment of the entire Russian army.

name: Memorial to Russian and French fallen at Valutino
description: A wooden cross and a tomb to the unknown soldier was placed at this place of the battlefield of Valutnio.

name: General Gudin burrial place
description: General Gudin was fatally wounded at the age of 44 and was evacuated to the Smolensk hospital, where his leg was amputated. He died a few days later despite treatment. By Napoleon's order, Gudin was buried in a single grave on one of the bastions of the Royal Fortress, to the right of the entrance to the fortification.

name: Altar of the Battle of Lubino
description: At this place was kept the Smolensk Icon of the Mother of God Hodegetria in 1812 to protect the Russian Army during the battle.

name: Memorial to the soldiers who fell at the Battle of Lubino
description: At this place was kept the Smolensk Icon of the Mother of God Hodegetria in 1812 to protect the Russian Army during the battle.

name: Monument to defenders of Smolensk
description: Commissioned by Emperor Nicholas I and designed by architect Antonio Adamini, this cast-iron chapel-style structure was unveiled on November 5, 1841, to commemorate the 29th anniversary of the city's liberation from Napoleon's forces.

name: Heroes' Memorial Square
description: opened in 1912 by Emperor Nicholas II to celebrate the centenary of the Patriotic War of 1812 against Napoleon, it is  nestled directly along the ancient Smolensk Fortress wall in the center of Smolensk.

name: Grateful Russia to the Heroes of 1812
description: Also known as the Eagle Monument, features two eagles on a massive boulder defending their nest from a sword-wielding warrior, symbolizing the unified Russian armies resisting Napoleon's forces.

name: General Anton Antonovich Skalon grave
description: Erected in 1912, by his grandchildren to mark the centennial of the 1812 Patriotic War. On August 5th 1812, aiming to prevent the French attack, Skalon attacked quickly, but was killed on the spot in the Battle of Smolensk, which pushed his force into retreat. His body fell into enemy hands and at Napoleon's personal command it was buried with full military honours three days after the French occupation of Smolensk.

name: Dormition Cathedral in Smolensk
description: During the 1812 Battle of Smolensk, the retreating Russian army took the city's highly venerated icon, Our Lady of Smolensk, to protect it from the invading forces. Napoleon himself ordered guards to protect the cathedral from being looted or completely destroyed by the fires ravaging the city.

name: Tyrolean freedom fighters memorial
description: The memorial site in front of the Parish of St. John the Baptist in Dorf Tirol (Tirolo) is a local war commemorative plaque and gravesite dedicated to the Tyrolean freedom fighters who fell during the historic 1809 rebellion against Napoleonic, French, and Bavarian forces

name: Colonel Jacques Henry Baltazar d'Arcy's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 01, avenue Thirion, 1ère ligne, M=AH-15), Paris
description: He commenced his career as a lieutenant in the 6th Line Infantry Regiment in 1803 and rose to Colonel in 1813.

name: General Joseph de Barbanègre's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 28, chemin du Dragon, 6ème ligne, M=R-32), Paris
description: Initially a sailor, then a captain in the 5th Battalion of the Lower Pyrenees, and Battalion Chief in the Consular Guard, but it was defending Fortress of Huningue against some 25.000 Austrians in 1815 which made him most famous, holding out with only several hundred men.

name: General Pierre Barrois's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 28, chemin Saint-Louis, 2ème ligne), Paris
description: He serve in all Coallition wars but the Fifth as he was serving in Spain. He is burried in the Leveque de Vilmorin family vault.

name: General Joseph de Barbanègre Birthplace
description: Joseph de Barbanègre was a French division general and Baron of the Empire who was born in Pontacq on August 22, 1772.

name: General Joseph de Barbanègre statue
description: The monument was crafted by the renowned sculptor Laurent-Honoré Marqueste and officially unveiled on August 16, 1896. To honor the bicentennial of the historic Siege of Huningue, the statue underwent a complete restoration in September 2015.

name: General Barbanègre's brothers tomb
description: Resting place preserves the memory of his brave brothers who also fought fiercely during the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars. Colonel Jean Barbanègre, a former Horse Grenadier of the Imperial Guard who participated in the historic Egyptian Campaign and survived the Battle of the Pyramides, only to fall heroically at the Battle of Jena in 1806.Jacques Barbanègre, an accomplished Chef d'escadron (Squadron Leader) who volunteered in 1793 and fought across Europe from Austerlitz to Waterloo before passing away in 1844.

name: Huningue garrisson sieges
description: The French garrison was besieged in 1814 and 1815.General Joseph Barbanègre, commanding the Huningue garrison, resisted for two months with a few hundred men to a large Austrian force of Archduke John.

name: General Henri François Baudrand's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 44, chemin du Quinconce, 14ème ligne, M=M-17), Paris
description: During the First Empire, Marie Étienne François Henri Baudrand served as a distinguished military engineer and staff officer across Italy, the Ionian Islands, and the Waterloo campaign.

name: General La Bonninière's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 28, chemin Masséna, 2ème ligne, M=P-33), Paris
description: During the First Empire, Marc-Antoine Bonnin de la Bonninière de Beaumont was a prominent cavalry general who led a division of dragoons across major Napoleonic campaigns.

name: General Augustin Belliard Birthplace
description: Augustin Daniel Belliard was born on May 25th 1769 in Fontenay-le-Comte, Vendée. His career mirrored the Napoleonic epic: he was practically involved in all the campaigns where he distinguished himself through numerous feats of arms.

name: General Augustin Belliard bust
description: A bust was erected in Place Belliard in 1836, in front of his birthplace. Removed in 1898, it was reinstalled in 1907 during a sumptuous ceremony.

name: Belliard Museum
description: Exhibition relating to the period of the First Empire and to the Napoleonic General Augustin-Daniel Belliard. ( open on July 14th and during Heritage Days, as well as by appointment made at the town hall secretariat)

name: General Augustin Belliard's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 35, avenue des Acacias, 3ème ligne, M=M-34), Paris
description: He passed away on January 28, 1832. At the time, he was serving as the French Ambassador to Belgium. He collapsed just after leaving the royal palace following a meeting with the Belgian King, Leopold I.

name: General Belliard's monument
description: The Statue of General Belliard holds a unique place in Belgian history as the very first monument ever inaugurated in the capital of the newly independent Kingdom of Belgium. Unveiled on September 23, 1838, the monument serves as a direct symbol of international support for the young nation.Grateful for his diplomatic interventions, the Belgian public funded the monument through an open public subscription.

name: Battle of Castelfranco Veneto
description: The ancestral home of the Bonaparte family and the birthplace of Napoleon Bonaparte.

name: General Sigismond-Frédéric de Berckheim's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 24, chemin de la Citerne, 1ère ligne), Paris
description: He joined an infantry regiment at the age of 14. In 1807 he became the commanding officer of the 1st Cuirassier Regiment. In 1809 he led his cavalrymen at Eckmühl, Ratisbon, Aspern-Essling and Wagram. He died at Paris on December 28th 1819.

name: Battle of Stecken memorial
description: Memorial to the battle of Stecken fought on December 5th 1805.

name: Battle of Stecken
description: Fought on December 5th 1805, resulting in an Austrian victory over Napoleon's Bavarian allies. Fought just a few days after the major French victory at Austerlitz—though the engaged forces were initially unaware of that outcome—it involved a surprise Austrian counter-attack led by Prince Friedrich of Hohenzollern-Hechingen and Archduke Ferdinand against Bavarian forces commanded by Carl Philipp von Wrede.

name: Battle of Wonau
description: The Battle of Wonau (also known as the action or skirmish of Wonau) was a minor engagement fought on December 2nd 1805, resulting in an Austrian victory over Bavarian forces allied with France. Wrede, commanding the 3rd and 5th Bavarian brigades, had the duty of protecting Napoleon's flank.

name: Battle of Lippa
description: The Battle of Lippa was a minor rearguard engagement fought on December 6th 1805 occurring just four days after Napoleon's decisive triumph at the Battle of Austerlitz

name: Battle of St. Mathia
description: This was the last clash for the campaign, between French and Austrian forces fought on December 9th 1805.

name: Battle of Prenzlau
description: In the Battle of Prenzlau or Capitulation of Prenzlau on October 28th 1806 two divisions of French cavalry and some infantry led by Marshal Joachim Murat intercepted a retreating Prussian corps led by Frederick Louis, Prince of Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen.

name: Battle of Vimeiro monument
description: It was inaugurated on August 21st 1908, to celebrate the first centennial of the historic Battle of Vimeiro, and was attended by Portugal's last monarch, King Manuel II, alongside the Minister of War.

name: Portuguese Soldier of the Peninsular War
description: The monument honors the role of Portuguese soldiers in the fight against Napoleonic troops in the historic Battle of Vimeiro. Work of Hélder Silva and Fernando Sarzedas, it was erected in 2007 in the area where decisive clashes took place in the Battle of Vimeiro. (Photo: Alta Falisa)

name: Battle of Vimeiro Field Hospital
description: This house, now in ruins, served precisely as the main medical point (Hospital de Sangue) to care for the wounded soldiers during the battle.

name: Wellington's HQ at Vimeiro
description: This house served as Sir Arthur Wellesley's headquarters during the battle of Vimeiro. The armistice that later would be the basis  to the agreement signed at Sintra for the final evacuation of the French from Portugal was negotiated and signed here.

name: Church of Vimeiro
description: During the Battle of Vimeiro on August 21, 1808, a fierce, bloody clash erupted around the local church when French forces under General Junot, failing to take the main British ridge, redirected their assault into the town where hand-to-hand combat ended in a French retreat.

name: Siege of Breslau
description: The siege of Breslau began on December 7th 1806, when General Vandamme ordered the opening of the first trenches and fire batteries near the suburb of Saint Nicolas. The city formally surrendered on January 3rd 1807, with the garrison's departure as prisoners of war agreed upon for January 7th.

name: Siege of Gaeta
description: The fortress city of Gaeta and its Neapolitan garrison under General Louis of Hesse-Philippsthal were besieged from February 26th to July 18th 1806 by an Imperial French corps led by Marshal André Masséna. After a prolonged defense in which Hesse was severely wounded, Gaeta surrendered, and Masséna granted its garrison generous terms.

name: Siege of Ragusa
description: After French occupied the maritime republic of Ragusa, Russian and allied forces under the leadership of Vice Admiral Dmitry Senyavin laid siege to it for months.

name: Marshal Ney's statue
description: Sculpted by François Rude and unveiled on December 7th 1853 stands where the famous Marshal, called 'the bravest of the brave' by Napoleon himself, was executed by a Bourbonic firing squad for treason in 1815.

name: Marshal Ney, December 7, 1815
description: Sculpted by Henri Alfred Jacquemart in 1868.

name: The Execution of Marshal Ney
description: The painting, by the French artist Jean-Léon Gérôme, has been owned by the Sheffield Galleries and Museums Trust since 1931, and is now in the collection of the Graves Art Gallery in Sheffield, England.

name: Invaion of Capri
description: The invasion of Capri was the successful recapture of the Italian island of Capri from Britain by the Kingdom of Naples on 4–18 October 1808.

name: Napoleon assassination attempt at Schönbrunn
description: On October 12th 1809, a young German theology student named Friedrich Staps attempted to assassinate Napoleon in the gardens of Schönbrunn Palace, where the Emperor was holding court. Staps, armed with a large dagger, was arrested before he could reach Napoleon, and later executed.

name: Mont-Dauphin POW camp
description: Mont-Dauphin operated as a prison in tandem with the nearby, larger fortress at Briançon. These high-altitude outposts formed a secure regional prison network isolated by hundreds of miles from France's northern and eastern frontier camps. The French authorities predominantly funneled non-British soldiers fighting under the British flag—most notably German mercenaries—to Mont-Dauphin. The Maltese corp captured in Capri in 1808 were imprisoned here.

name: Isla Cabrera POW camp
description: The island of Cabrera (Balearic Islands) served between 1809 and 1814 as an infamous natural prison camp for some 11,000 soldiers of Napoleon's army captured at the Battle of Bailén.

name: Murat Ordering the Capture of Capri
description: The canvas 'Murat Ordering the Capture of Capri in 1808' was painted by the German artist Johann Heinrich Schmidt in 1811. The original oil on canvas artwork is housed at the Musée Marmottan Monet in Paris, France.

name: Invaion of Capri - Marina Piccola landing
description: A diversionary attack on the port of Marina Piccola was executed with 540 troops landing at that point.

name: Invaion of Capri - Marina Grande landing
description: A diversionary attack on the port of Marina Grande was executed with 480 troops landing at that point.

name: Invaion of Capri - Fort Orico landing
description: This was the primary zone of the main assault. Neapolitan and French troops managed to scale the sheer cliffs here by using ladders famously borrowed from the streetlamp-lighters of Naples.

name: Invaion of Capri - Cala di Mezzo landing
description: Neapolitan and French troops landed in this cove near the southwestern tip of the island to breach the British line of defenses.

name: Invaion of Capri - Fort Mesola
description: Positioned between Pino and Orrico, this fortified point on the Campetiello promontory was aggressively stormed immediately following the initial landings.

name: Napoléon Bonaparte, Premier Consul
description: Napoléon Bonaparte, Premier Consul is an oil-on-canvas portrait painted by French artist Joseph Franque during the French Consulate period (1799-1804).

name: Promenade de Napoléon et M.Louise à Fontainebleau
description: Promenade de Napoléon et de Marie-Louise à Fontainebleau (1810) is a grand-scale, collaborative oil painting on canvas by renowned French artists Jean-Joseph-Xavier Bidauld and Louis-Léopold Boilly.

name: Départ de Napoléon et de M.Louise pour la chasse au château de Compiègne
description: Départ de Napoléon Ier et Marie-Louise pour la chasse au château de Compiègne (1811) is a tall, narrow oil-on-canvas painting created through the collaboration of French masters Jean-Joseph-Xavier Bidauld and Carle Vernet.

name: Promenade de Napoléon et M.Louise au château de Saint-Cloud
description: Promenade de Napoléon Ier et de Marie-Louise au château de Saint-Cloud (1811) is a tall, narrow oil-on-canvas painting created through a master-level collaboration between French landscape painter Jean-Joseph-Xavier Bidauld and renowned equestrian artist Carle Vernet.

name: Murat's HQ during he invasion of Capri
description: In October 1808, Joachim Murat, King of Naples, made this Villa his headquarters to command the siege and recapture of Capri from British forces allied with the Bourbons. He chose the site for its strategic vantage point, telling his generals it provided the best view of the sea around Capri to track the battle in real time.

name: Murat, King of Naples, Watches the Capture of Capri
location: Museo della Certosa di San Martino, Naples
description: This historical painting by Odoardo Fischetti, painted between 1809 and 1811, captures King Joachim Murat of Naples directing the October 1808 military assault to recapture the island of Capri from British forces.

name: Capture of Cairo
description: Napoleon captured Cairo on July 22nd 1798, following his decisive victory over the Mamluk army at the Battle of the Pyramids on July 21st.

name: The Battle of Alexandria (sketch canvas)
location: National Army Museum, Study Collection, London
description: 'The Battle of Alexandria, 21 March 1801' is a dramatic oil on canvas painted by Robert Ker Porter around 1801. This vigorous sketch captures the night battle between French and British forces and served as a preparatory study for a massive, now-lost panoramic painting.

name: The Battle of Alexandria (canvas)
location: National Army Museum, Study Collection, London
description: Oil on canvas after Philippe Jacques de Loutherbourg (1740-1812), 1805 (c).

name: The Flag (canvas)
location: National Army Museum, Study Collection, London
description: Painted by William Barnes Wollen in 1912, 'The Flag (Albuhera, May 16, 1811)', recreates the historic defense of the British 3rd Regiment of Foot's colors during the brutal Battle of Albuera.

name: National Army Museum
description: The National Army Museum in Chelsea, London, holds extensive collections documenting the British Army's involvement in the Peninsular War (1808–1814), featuring personal archives, uniform items, fine art, and campaign relics from the Duke of Wellington's campaigns in Spain and Portugal and Waterloo.

name: Dawn of Waterloo
location: National Army Museum, Myth and Reality, London
description: Oil on canvas by renowned British military painter Lady Butler (Elizabeth Southerden Butler, née Thompson), signed with initials and dated lower left '18 EB 95'. Created in 1895, this work was exhibited that same year at the Royal Academy of Arts in London.

name: The 28th Regiment at Quatre Bras
description: The 28th Regiment at Quatre Bras is a famous 1875 oil-on-canvas historical battle painting by the renowned British military artist Elizabeth Thompson (later known as Lady Butler).

name: General César Berthier's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 53, chemin du Bastion, 6ème ligne, M=U-13), Paris
description: Brother of Louis-Alexandre Berthier the Empire maréchal, the division general Victor Léopold Berthier, and maréchal de camp Joseph-Alexandre Berthier, 1st Viscount Berthier (1821).

name: General Victor Berthier's tomb
location: Père Lachaise Cemetery (Division 11, chemin Denon, 3ème ligne, M=X-22), Paris
description: Brother of Marshal Louis-Alexandre, he served during the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, rising to the rank of general of division.

name: Blücher Museum
description: Housed at Blücher's headquarters at that time, the main theme of the museum is the crossing of the Rhine by the Silesian Army, which, after the Battle of Leipzig in the first week of New Year's 1814, crossed the Rhine on a Russian pontoon bridge at the nearby Pfalz under the Prussian Field Marshal Blücher.

name: Blücher Memorial Stone
description: The memorial stone, unveiled on November 1853, commemorates the Prussian Field Marshal Blücher for his spectacular crossing of the Rhine on New Year's Eve 1813/1814.

name: Blücher Statue at Kaub
description: This bronze statue of Marshal Blücher sculpted in 1893 by the prominent Berlin sculptor Prof. Friedrich Schaper was unveiled on June 18, 1894 to mark the anniversary of the Battle of Waterloo. Generalfeldmarschall Blücher is depicted in the military uniform he wore during the German Wars of Liberation (1813-1815).

name: Russian Ulhan Regiment Memorial
description: This memorial was erected on November 6th 1912 to honor the Regiment of Uhlans who distinguished themselves in the battles of 1812.

name: Battle of Krasnoi Memorial
description: This memorial Cross dedicated to the 100th anniversary of the Battle of Krasnoi was first laid down and inaugurated in 1912 to mark the exact centennial anniversary of the battle. During the Soviet era, the monument suffered severe neglect, but the square and the historical memorial cross complex were fully restored and updated in the post-Soviet period.

name: Battle of Krasnoi Column
description: It was originally designed by the Swiss architect Antonio Adamini and first erected in 1847 to commemorate the fierce battles of November 1812, where Russian troops ambushed Napoleon's weakened Grande Armée during its retreat. Although the original cast-iron structure was destroyed in the 1930s during the Soviet era, an exact replica was rebuilt and opened in 2012 to celebrate the bicentenary of the war.

name: Blücher's crossing of the Rhine (1859)
description: The 1859 oil on Wood artwork done by Wilhelm Camphausen is housed in the Mittelrhein-Museum in Koblenz. In this first verion a dense group of civilian spectators and children standing closely on the right bank.

name: Blücher's crossing of the Rhine (1860)
description: The 1860 oil on canvas by Wilhelm Camphausen is a second and larger version of Blücher crossing of the Rhine scene. In this second verion the civilian crowd is significantly minimized, focusing much heavier attention on rows of uniformed soldiers.
